# SiteForge Software Development Specification

> Searchable implementation companion to `SiteForge-Specification.docx`. The DOCX remains the editable publication copy.

SITEFORGE

Native macOS visual website builder and portable web publishing system

Version 1.0  •  Baseline source of truth  •  18 July 2026

| Document status | Implementation baseline — proposed |
| --- | --- |
| Normative scope | macOS editor, project model, preview/runtime, export, quality system, extensibility, delivery |
| Primary audience | Product, design, architecture, engineering, QA, security, accessibility, documentation, AI implementation agents |
| Requirement policy | MUST = release obligation; SHOULD = expected unless waived; MAY = optional capability |
| Ownership | Product and Engineering jointly; module owners assigned during planning |

Purpose

This document is the authoritative behavioral and engineering contract for an AI-assisted, human-reviewed implementation. It is deliberately explicit about state, failure, recovery, verification, and release evidence.

## Document Control

This specification is a living baseline. Changes to normative behavior require a versioned change proposal, impact analysis, approval by the accountable product and engineering owners, and updates to linked tests and implementation records.

| Version | Date | Status | Change summary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0.1 | 2026-07-18 | Draft | Initial comprehensive structure and requirements baseline |
| 0.9 | TBD | Review | Cross-functional review and unresolved-decision closure |
| 1.0 | TBD | Approved | Implementation baseline |

## How to Use This Specification

- Treat every requirement identifier as stable. If wording changes without changing intent, retain the ID. If intent changes materially, supersede the old requirement and create a new one.
- Build work packets around a bounded set of requirement IDs. A packet includes relevant model contracts, UI states, failure behavior, acceptance criteria, test obligations, and architecture decisions.
- Do not infer omitted behavior from a competitor. Record an open decision or change proposal. Reference implementations may inform research but do not override this specification.
- A feature is not complete when the happy path renders. Completion requires persistence, undo/redo, accessibility, diagnostics, performance, security, migration, and verification appropriate to its risk.
- AI-generated code must be reviewed by a human owner, linked to requirements, tested at the lowest effective layer, and checked for architectural drift before merge.
## Normative Conventions

MUST and MUST NOT are release obligations. SHOULD and SHOULD NOT are expected behavior; deviation requires a documented, time-bounded exception. MAY identifies an optional extension. “System” means the SiteForge product unless a narrower subsystem is named. “User” includes keyboard-only and assistive-technology users.

## Definition of Done — Every User-Facing Capability

- Behavior matches its requirement and acceptance criteria.
- Mutations participate in transactions, autosave, undo/redo, recovery, and version comparison as applicable.
- Keyboard access, VoiceOver semantics, focus behavior, localization, and reduced-motion behavior are verified.
- Error, empty, loading, offline, permission-denied, and unsupported states are intentionally designed.
- Diagnostics identify failures without leaking project content or secrets.
- Performance is measured on named fixtures and reference hardware.
- Automated tests and manual evidence are linked in traceability records.
- Documentation and migration notes are updated.

## I. Product Foundation

This part is normative. Module introductions establish scope; numbered requirements define verifiable obligations. Cross-cutting requirements in Quality Attributes and Testing apply even when not repeated in a module.

### 1.1 Product vision and boundaries

Module code  0101

Defines the product promise, target outcomes, competitive posture, explicit non-goals, and the boundary between authoring, hosting, and collaboration.

#### Scope and Outcomes

- Primary objects: workspace, project, site, page, node, style, breakpoint, build.
- Primary user outcomes: create a production-ready site; move from idea to published output; preserve user ownership; avoid hidden lock-in.
- Critical invariant: product intent remains stable across implementation choices; user content is portable; local authoring remains useful without a service.
- The module includes authoring UI, model semantics, persistence, history, preview/export behavior, accessibility, diagnostics, migrations, and verification unless explicitly excluded.
- The module excludes connected-service implementation details that are not needed for local authoring; those are handled behind adapters and permission boundaries.
#### Behavioral Model

The model for product vision and boundaries is authoritative and UI-independent. Editing uses a draft → validate → preview → commit sequence. A commit creates one transaction with an operation name, actor, timestamp, affected stable identifiers, and an inverse or restoration strategy. Background work consumes immutable snapshots and returns results tagged with the originating revision; stale results are ignored.

All controls show whether a value is authored, inherited, calculated, unavailable, or mixed. When multiple selections are involved, the system computes the applicable subset before preview. It must not silently coerce incompatible objects. Removing a value restores the next valid source rather than writing a visually similar literal.

#### States and Edge Conditions

- Empty: explain the first useful action and provide it directly; do not display a dead panel.
- Loading or computing: retain last valid content when safe, show bounded progress, and allow cancellation for user-initiated work.
- Mixed or partially applicable: identify the affected subset and preserve differences until the user commits a unifying value.
- Invalid: retain the user’s draft separately, state the violated rule, and offer specific repair without replacing committed data.
- Missing dependency: preserve the reference and editable intent, use a defined fallback, and provide locate, replace, or detach actions.
- Read-only or denied: explain the governing policy and keep inspection, copy, and export available where permitted.
- Offline or service unavailable: keep local authoring operational; queue only idempotent connected operations and display their state.
- Large selection or project: virtualize and batch presentation while keeping the mutation atomic and cancelable.
#### Normative Requirements

##### SF-0101-001 — Authoritative state

Requirement  The system MUST represent this capability in the canonical project model with stable identity, explicit defaults, typed validation, and versioned serialization. The serialized representation MUST distinguish omitted, defaulted, and explicitly authored values for workspace.

Rationale  This requirement exists so that create a production-ready site remains predictable when the project grows, is reopened, is exported, or is operated through an accessibility path. The authoritative state is expressed through workspace; UI convenience state cannot become a second source of truth.

Acceptance criteria  The following observations are required:

- Given valid workspace state, performing the operation through pointer, keyboard, menu, or an applicable automation API commits one equivalent transaction and produces the specified result.
- Cancel, Escape, validation failure, permission denial, or subsystem interruption leaves the last committed document unchanged and provides a specific recovery action.
- Save, close, reopen, undo, redo, duplication, and version comparison preserve the result and its identity; product intent remains stable across implementation choices.
- Accessibility labels, focus order, announcements, and reduced-motion behavior expose the same capability without requiring pixel-precise pointer input.
- Diagnostics include requirement ID SF-0101-001, operation type, sanitized object identifiers, duration, and failure category; content values and secrets are excluded by default.
Verification  Unit tests cover resolution and invalid inputs; integration tests cover transaction and persistence boundaries; UI tests cover the primary journey and cancellation; exploratory QA covers scale, localization, accessibility, and recovery. Requirement owner records evidence in the traceability index.

Priority / milestone  MUST. Release blocking for the first milestone in which this module is enabled; later refinements may be separately scoped only when the mandatory path remains complete.

#### Module Acceptance Checklist

☐ A new user can complete: create a production-ready site; move from idea to published output; preserve user ownership; avoid hidden lock-in.

☐ Round-trip tests prove that workspace, project, site, page, node, style, breakpoint, build retain stable identity and intent.

☐ Undo and redo are correct across creation, edit, delete, bulk change, and dependency repair.

☐ Save during active editing, forced termination, reopen, and migration preserve the last committed state.

☐ VoiceOver, Full Keyboard Access, high contrast, reduced motion, and 200% UI scaling complete the core flow.

☐ Preview and exported output either match authoring semantics or surface a documented compatibility finding.

☐ Diagnostics and support bundles remain useful with project-content inclusion disabled.

☐ Performance budgets pass for standard and large fixtures on named minimum and reference hardware.

### 1.3 Success metrics and product telemetry

Module code  0103

Defines measurable quality, adoption, reliability, and workflow efficiency outcomes while preserving privacy.

#### Scope and Outcomes

- Primary objects: metric, event, session, funnel, cohort, consent, diagnostic sample.
- Primary user outcomes: measure time-to-first-publish; detect task failure; compare feature adoption; disable analytics; export diagnostic evidence.
- Critical invariant: metrics cannot become shadow requirements; telemetry is opt-in where legally required; content is excluded by default.
- The module includes authoring UI, model semantics, persistence, history, preview/export behavior, accessibility, diagnostics, migrations, and verification unless explicitly excluded.
- The module excludes connected-service implementation details that are not needed for local authoring; those are handled behind adapters and permission boundaries.
#### Behavioral Model

The model for success metrics and product telemetry is authoritative and UI-independent. Editing uses a draft → validate → preview → commit sequence. A commit creates one transaction with an operation name, actor, timestamp, affected stable identifiers, and an inverse or restoration strategy. Background work consumes immutable snapshots and returns results tagged with the originating revision; stale results are ignored.

All controls show whether a value is authored, inherited, calculated, unavailable, or mixed. When multiple selections are involved, the system computes the applicable subset before preview. It must not silently coerce incompatible objects. Removing a value restores the next valid source rather than writing a visually similar literal.

#### States and Edge Conditions

- Empty: explain the first useful action and provide it directly; do not display a dead panel.
- Loading or computing: retain last valid content when safe, show bounded progress, and allow cancellation for user-initiated work.
- Mixed or partially applicable: identify the affected subset and preserve differences until the user commits a unifying value.
- Invalid: retain the user’s draft separately, state the violated rule, and offer specific repair without replacing committed data.
- Missing dependency: preserve the reference and editable intent, use a defined fallback, and provide locate, replace, or detach actions.
- Read-only or denied: explain the governing policy and keep inspection, copy, and export available where permitted.
- Offline or service unavailable: keep local authoring operational; queue only idempotent connected operations and display their state.
- Large selection or project: virtualize and batch presentation while keeping the mutation atomic and cancelable.

### 1.5 Terminology and normative language

Module code  0105

Establishes canonical product terms and the meaning of MUST, SHOULD, MAY, acceptance criteria, and exceptions.

#### Scope and Outcomes

- Primary objects: term, definition, alias, requirement, constraint, decision, exception.
- Primary user outcomes: name objects consistently; distinguish authoring from runtime; resolve ambiguous language.
- Critical invariant: terms have one canonical meaning; aliases are documented; normative statements are testable.
- The module includes authoring UI, model semantics, persistence, history, preview/export behavior, accessibility, diagnostics, migrations, and verification unless explicitly excluded.
- The module excludes connected-service implementation details that are not needed for local authoring; those are handled behind adapters and permission boundaries.
#### Behavioral Model

The model for terminology and normative language is authoritative and UI-independent. Editing uses a draft → validate → preview → commit sequence. A commit creates one transaction with an operation name, actor, timestamp, affected stable identifiers, and an inverse or restoration strategy. Background work consumes immutable snapshots and returns results tagged with the originating revision; stale results are ignored.

All controls show whether a value is authored, inherited, calculated, unavailable, or mixed. When multiple selections are involved, the system computes the applicable subset before preview. It must not silently coerce incompatible objects. Removing a value restores the next valid source rather than writing a visually similar literal.

#### States and Edge Conditions

- Empty: explain the first useful action and provide it directly; do not display a dead panel.
- Loading or computing: retain last valid content when safe, show bounded progress, and allow cancellation for user-initiated work.
- Mixed or partially applicable: identify the affected subset and preserve differences until the user commits a unifying value.
- Invalid: retain the user’s draft separately, state the violated rule, and offer specific repair without replacing committed data.
- Missing dependency: preserve the reference and editable intent, use a defined fallback, and provide locate, replace, or detach actions.
- Read-only or denied: explain the governing policy and keep inspection, copy, and export available where permitted.
- Offline or service unavailable: keep local authoring operational; queue only idempotent connected operations and display their state.
- Large selection or project: virtualize and batch presentation while keeping the mutation atomic and cancelable.
#### Normative Requirements

##### SF-0105-001 — Authoritative state

Requirement  The system MUST represent this capability in the canonical project model with stable identity, explicit defaults, typed validation, and versioned serialization. The serialized representation MUST distinguish omitted, defaulted, and explicitly authored values for term.

Rationale  This requirement exists so that name objects consistently remains predictable when the project grows, is reopened, is exported, or is operated through an accessibility path. The authoritative state is expressed through term; UI convenience state cannot become a second source of truth.

Acceptance criteria  The following observations are required:

- Given valid term state, performing the operation through pointer, keyboard, menu, or an applicable automation API commits one equivalent transaction and produces the specified result.
- Cancel, Escape, validation failure, permission denial, or subsystem interruption leaves the last committed document unchanged and provides a specific recovery action.
- Save, close, reopen, undo, redo, duplication, and version comparison preserve the result and its identity; terms have one canonical meaning.
- Accessibility labels, focus order, announcements, and reduced-motion behavior expose the same capability without requiring pixel-precise pointer input.
- Diagnostics include requirement ID SF-0105-001, operation type, sanitized object identifiers, duration, and failure category; content values and secrets are excluded by default.
Verification  Unit tests cover resolution and invalid inputs; integration tests cover transaction and persistence boundaries; UI tests cover the primary journey and cancellation; exploratory QA covers scale, localization, accessibility, and recovery. Requirement owner records evidence in the traceability index.

Priority / milestone  MUST. Release blocking for the first milestone in which this module is enabled; later refinements may be separately scoped only when the mandatory path remains complete.

### 2.2 Navigation and information architecture

Module code  0202

Defines how users move between project, page, component, CMS, asset, publishing, and settings contexts.

#### Scope and Outcomes

- Primary objects: route, context, breadcrumb, back stack, deep link, recent item.
- Primary user outcomes: switch contexts without losing selection; deep-link to an object; return to prior work.
- Critical invariant: navigation never mutates content; unavailable destinations explain why.
- The module includes authoring UI, model semantics, persistence, history, preview/export behavior, accessibility, diagnostics, migrations, and verification unless explicitly excluded.
- The module excludes connected-service implementation details that are not needed for local authoring; those are handled behind adapters and permission boundaries.
#### Behavioral Model

The model for navigation and information architecture is authoritative and UI-independent. Editing uses a draft → validate → preview → commit sequence. A commit creates one transaction with an operation name, actor, timestamp, affected stable identifiers, and an inverse or restoration strategy. Background work consumes immutable snapshots and returns results tagged with the originating revision; stale results are ignored.

All controls show whether a value is authored, inherited, calculated, unavailable, or mixed. When multiple selections are involved, the system computes the applicable subset before preview. It must not silently coerce incompatible objects. Removing a value restores the next valid source rather than writing a visually similar literal.

#### States and Edge Conditions

- Empty: explain the first useful action and provide it directly; do not display a dead panel.
- Loading or computing: retain last valid content when safe, show bounded progress, and allow cancellation for user-initiated work.
- Mixed or partially applicable: identify the affected subset and preserve differences until the user commits a unifying value.
- Invalid: retain the user’s draft separately, state the violated rule, and offer specific repair without replacing committed data.
- Missing dependency: preserve the reference and editable intent, use a defined fallback, and provide locate, replace, or detach actions.
- Read-only or denied: explain the governing policy and keep inspection, copy, and export available where permitted.
- Offline or service unavailable: keep local authoring operational; queue only idempotent connected operations and display their state.
- Large selection or project: virtualize and batch presentation while keeping the mutation atomic and cancelable.
#### Normative Requirements

##### SF-0202-001 — Authoritative state

Requirement  The system MUST represent this capability in the canonical project model with stable identity, explicit defaults, typed validation, and versioned serialization. The serialized representation MUST distinguish omitted, defaulted, and explicitly authored values for route.

Rationale  This requirement exists so that switch contexts without losing selection remains predictable when the project grows, is reopened, is exported, or is operated through an accessibility path. The authoritative state is expressed through route; UI convenience state cannot become a second source of truth.

Acceptance criteria  The following observations are required:

- Given valid route state, performing the operation through pointer, keyboard, menu, or an applicable automation API commits one equivalent transaction and produces the specified result.
- Cancel, Escape, validation failure, permission denial, or subsystem interruption leaves the last committed document unchanged and provides a specific recovery action.
- Save, close, reopen, undo, redo, duplication, and version comparison preserve the result and its identity; navigation never mutates content.
- Accessibility labels, focus order, announcements, and reduced-motion behavior expose the same capability without requiring pixel-precise pointer input.
- Diagnostics include requirement ID SF-0202-001, operation type, sanitized object identifiers, duration, and failure category; content values and secrets are excluded by default.
Verification  Unit tests cover resolution and invalid inputs; integration tests cover transaction and persistence boundaries; UI tests cover the primary journey and cancellation; exploratory QA covers scale, localization, accessibility, and recovery. Requirement owner records evidence in the traceability index.

### 2.5 Search, command palette, and quick open

Module code  0205

Defines cross-project search, in-project object search, actions, filters, ranking, and navigation.

#### Scope and Outcomes

- Primary objects: query, result, scope, filter, recent, command, index.
- Primary user outcomes: find pages and nodes; execute a command; filter by object type; reveal a result.
- Critical invariant: search results reflect saved and current in-memory state; private content stays local unless consented.
- The module includes authoring UI, model semantics, persistence, history, preview/export behavior, accessibility, diagnostics, migrations, and verification unless explicitly excluded.
- The module excludes connected-service implementation details that are not needed for local authoring; those are handled behind adapters and permission boundaries.
#### Behavioral Model

The model for search, command palette, and quick open is authoritative and UI-independent. Editing uses a draft → validate → preview → commit sequence. A commit creates one transaction with an operation name, actor, timestamp, affected stable identifiers, and an inverse or restoration strategy. Background work consumes immutable snapshots and returns results tagged with the originating revision; stale results are ignored.

All controls show whether a value is authored, inherited, calculated, unavailable, or mixed. When multiple selections are involved, the system computes the applicable subset before preview. It must not silently coerce incompatible objects. Removing a value restores the next valid source rather than writing a visually similar literal.

#### States and Edge Conditions

- Empty: explain the first useful action and provide it directly; do not display a dead panel.
- Loading or computing: retain last valid content when safe, show bounded progress, and allow cancellation for user-initiated work.
- Mixed or partially applicable: identify the affected subset and preserve differences until the user commits a unifying value.
- Invalid: retain the user’s draft separately, state the violated rule, and offer specific repair without replacing committed data.
- Missing dependency: preserve the reference and editable intent, use a defined fallback, and provide locate, replace, or detach actions.
- Read-only or denied: explain the governing policy and keep inspection, copy, and export available where permitted.
- Offline or service unavailable: keep local authoring operational; queue only idempotent connected operations and display their state.
- Large selection or project: virtualize and batch presentation while keeping the mutation atomic and cancelable.

## III. Document and Project Model

This part is normative. Module introductions establish scope; numbered requirements define verifiable obligations. Cross-cutting requirements in Quality Attributes and Testing apply even when not repeated in a module.

### 3.1 Project lifecycle and storage

Module code  0301

Defines creation, open, close, duplicate, move, archive, autosave, recovery, and package layout.

#### Scope and Outcomes

- Primary objects: project package, manifest, document, resource, snapshot, lock, migration.
- Primary user outcomes: create and open a project; recover after interruption; duplicate safely; inspect package contents.
- Critical invariant: the project is atomic from the user perspective; partial writes cannot corrupt the last known-good state.
- The module includes authoring UI, model semantics, persistence, history, preview/export behavior, accessibility, diagnostics, migrations, and verification unless explicitly excluded.
- The module excludes connected-service implementation details that are not needed for local authoring; those are handled behind adapters and permission boundaries.
#### Behavioral Model

The model for project lifecycle and storage is authoritative and UI-independent. Editing uses a draft → validate → preview → commit sequence. A commit creates one transaction with an operation name, actor, timestamp, affected stable identifiers, and an inverse or restoration strategy. Background work consumes immutable snapshots and returns results tagged with the originating revision; stale results are ignored.

All controls show whether a value is authored, inherited, calculated, unavailable, or mixed. When multiple selections are involved, the system computes the applicable subset before preview. It must not silently coerce incompatible objects. Removing a value restores the next valid source rather than writing a visually similar literal.

#### States and Edge Conditions

- Empty: explain the first useful action and provide it directly; do not display a dead panel.
- Loading or computing: retain last valid content when safe, show bounded progress, and allow cancellation for user-initiated work.
- Mixed or partially applicable: identify the affected subset and preserve differences until the user commits a unifying value.
- Invalid: retain the user’s draft separately, state the violated rule, and offer specific repair without replacing committed data.
- Missing dependency: preserve the reference and editable intent, use a defined fallback, and provide locate, replace, or detach actions.
- Read-only or denied: explain the governing policy and keep inspection, copy, and export available where permitted.
- Offline or service unavailable: keep local authoring operational; queue only idempotent connected operations and display their state.
- Large selection or project: virtualize and batch presentation while keeping the mutation atomic and cancelable.

### 3.3 Pages, routes, and site hierarchy

Module code  0303

Defines pages, folders, route segments, home and error pages, dynamic routes, redirects, and navigation metadata.

Approved blank-project baseline (`OD-003`, 2026-07-19): create Home at `/`, followed by Not Found at `/404`; assign the home and error-page roles respectively; give each page exactly one minimum valid root node; and add no sample text, sections, or template content. Creation of this structure is one clean project baseline and remains distinct from template creation.

#### Scope and Outcomes

- Primary objects: page, folder, route, slug, redirect, locale, route parameter.
- Primary user outcomes: create static and dynamic pages; reorder hierarchy; validate routes; preview navigation.
- Critical invariant: published routes are unique per locale; reserved paths are protected; redirects cannot form loops.
- The module includes authoring UI, model semantics, persistence, history, preview/export behavior, accessibility, diagnostics, migrations, and verification unless explicitly excluded.
- The module excludes connected-service implementation details that are not needed for local authoring; those are handled behind adapters and permission boundaries.
#### Behavioral Model

The model for pages, routes, and site hierarchy is authoritative and UI-independent. Editing uses a draft → validate → preview → commit sequence. A commit creates one transaction with an operation name, actor, timestamp, affected stable identifiers, and an inverse or restoration strategy. Background work consumes immutable snapshots and returns results tagged with the originating revision; stale results are ignored.

All controls show whether a value is authored, inherited, calculated, unavailable, or mixed. When multiple selections are involved, the system computes the applicable subset before preview. It must not silently coerce incompatible objects. Removing a value restores the next valid source rather than writing a visually similar literal.

#### States and Edge Conditions

- Empty: explain the first useful action and provide it directly; do not display a dead panel.
- Loading or computing: retain last valid content when safe, show bounded progress, and allow cancellation for user-initiated work.
- Mixed or partially applicable: identify the affected subset and preserve differences until the user commits a unifying value.
- Invalid: retain the user’s draft separately, state the violated rule, and offer specific repair without replacing committed data.
- Missing dependency: preserve the reference and editable intent, use a defined fallback, and provide locate, replace, or detach actions.
- Read-only or denied: explain the governing policy and keep inspection, copy, and export available where permitted.
- Offline or service unavailable: keep local authoring operational; queue only idempotent connected operations and display their state.
- Large selection or project: virtualize and batch presentation while keeping the mutation atomic and cancelable.

The authoritative state is expressed through page; UI convenience state cannot become a second source of truth.

### 3.5 Properties, tokens, and value resolution

Module code  0305

Defines authored, inherited, responsive, state, variable, expression, and default values.

#### Scope and Outcomes

- Primary objects: property, literal, token, variable, expression, cascade, provenance.
- Primary user outcomes: set and clear values; bind tokens; inspect computed values; trace provenance.
- Critical invariant: computed values are deterministic; clearing restores the next valid source; cycles are diagnosed.
- The module includes authoring UI, model semantics, persistence, history, preview/export behavior, accessibility, diagnostics, migrations, and verification unless explicitly excluded.
- The module excludes connected-service implementation details that are not needed for local authoring; those are handled behind adapters and permission boundaries.
#### Behavioral Model

The model for properties, tokens, and value resolution is authoritative and UI-independent. Editing uses a draft → validate → preview → commit sequence. A commit creates one transaction with an operation name, actor, timestamp, affected stable identifiers, and an inverse or restoration strategy. Background work consumes immutable snapshots and returns results tagged with the originating revision; stale results are ignored.

All controls show whether a value is authored, inherited, calculated, unavailable, or mixed. When multiple selections are involved, the system computes the applicable subset before preview. It must not silently coerce incompatible objects. Removing a value restores the next valid source rather than writing a visually similar literal.

#### States and Edge Conditions

- Empty: explain the first useful action and provide it directly; do not display a dead panel.
- Loading or computing: retain last valid content when safe, show bounded progress, and allow cancellation for user-initiated work.
- Mixed or partially applicable: identify the affected subset and preserve differences until the user commits a unifying value.
- Invalid: retain the user’s draft separately, state the violated rule, and offer specific repair without replacing committed data.
- Missing dependency: preserve the reference and editable intent, use a defined fallback, and provide locate, replace, or detach actions.
- Read-only or denied: explain the governing policy and keep inspection, copy, and export available where permitted.
- Offline or service unavailable: keep local authoring operational; queue only idempotent connected operations and display their state.
- Large selection or project: virtualize and batch presentation while keeping the mutation atomic and cancelable.

Requirement  The system MUST represent this capability in the canonical project model with stable identity, explicit defaults, typed validation, and versioned serialization. The serialized representation MUST distinguish omitted, defaulted, and explicitly authored values for property.

Rationale  This requirement exists so that set and clear values remains predictable when the project grows, is reopened, is exported, or is operated through an accessibility path. The authoritative state is expressed through property; UI convenience state cannot become a second source of truth.

Acceptance criteria  The following observations are required:

- Given valid property state, performing the operation through pointer, keyboard, menu, or an applicable automation API commits one equivalent transaction and produces the specified result.
- Cancel, Escape, validation failure, permission denial, or subsystem interruption leaves the last committed document unchanged and provides a specific recovery action.
- Save, close, reopen, undo, redo, duplication, and version comparison preserve the result and its identity; computed values are deterministic.
- Accessibility labels, focus order, announcements, and reduced-motion behavior expose the same capability without requiring pixel-precise pointer input.
- Diagnostics include requirement ID SF-0305-001, operation type, sanitized object identifiers, duration, and failure category; content values and secrets are excluded by default.
Verification  Unit tests cover resolution and invalid inputs; integration tests cover transaction and persistence boundaries; UI tests cover the primary journey and cancellation; exploratory QA covers scale, localization, accessibility, and recovery. ### 3.7 Undo, redo, and history

Module code  0307

Defines command grouping, coalescing, branching policy, selection restoration, named checkpoints, and history UI.

#### Scope and Outcomes

- Primary objects: history entry, inverse, coalescing key, checkpoint, branch, author.
- Primary user outcomes: undo typing and drags naturally; inspect history; revert to checkpoint; restore selection.
- Critical invariant: undo never produces an invalid document; remote and generated changes have explicit history treatment.
- The module includes authoring UI, model semantics, persistence, history, preview/export behavior, accessibility, diagnostics, migrations, and verification unless explicitly excluded.
- The module excludes connected-service implementation details that are not needed for local authoring; those are handled behind adapters and permission boundaries.
#### Behavioral Model

The model for undo, redo, and history is authoritative and UI-independent. Editing uses a draft → validate → preview → commit sequence. A commit creates one transaction with an operation name, actor, timestamp, affected stable identifiers, and an inverse or restoration strategy. Background work consumes immutable snapshots and returns results tagged with the originating revision; stale results are ignored.

All controls show whether a value is authored, inherited, calculated, unavailable, or mixed. When multiple selections are involved, the system computes the applicable subset before preview. It must not silently coerce incompatible objects. Removing a value restores the next valid source rather than writing a visually similar literal.

#### States and Edge Conditions

- Empty: explain the first useful action and provide it directly; do not display a dead panel.
- Loading or computing: retain last valid content when safe, show bounded progress, and allow cancellation for user-initiated work.
- Mixed or partially applicable: identify the affected subset and preserve differences until the user commits a unifying value.
- Invalid: retain the user’s draft separately, state the violated rule, and offer specific repair without replacing committed data.
- Missing dependency: preserve the reference and editable intent, use a defined fallback, and provide locate, replace, or detach actions.
- Read-only or denied: explain the governing policy and keep inspection, copy, and export available where permitted.
- Offline or service unavailable: keep local authoring operational; queue only idempotent connected operations and display their state.
- Large selection or project: virtualize and batch presentation while keeping the mutation atomic and cancelable.

### 3.9 Import and migration framework

Module code  0309

Defines import adapters, validation, previews, migrations, rollback, and compatibility reporting.

#### Scope and Outcomes

- Primary objects: importer, source format, mapping, warning, migration step, compatibility report.
- Primary user outcomes: import external assets and markup; preview mappings; migrate old projects; cancel safely.
- Critical invariant: imports are staged before commit; migrations are idempotent and preserve a recovery copy.
- The module includes authoring UI, model semantics, persistence, history, preview/export behavior, accessibility, diagnostics, migrations, and verification unless explicitly excluded.
- The module excludes connected-service implementation details that are not needed for local authoring; those are handled behind adapters and permission boundaries.
#### Behavioral Model

The model for import and migration framework is authoritative and UI-independent. Editing uses a draft → validate → preview → commit sequence. A commit creates one transaction with an operation name, actor, timestamp, affected stable identifiers, and an inverse or restoration strategy. Background work consumes immutable snapshots and returns results tagged with the originating revision; stale results are ignored.

All controls show whether a value is authored, inherited, calculated, unavailable, or mixed. When multiple selections are involved, the system computes the applicable subset before preview. It must not silently coerce incompatible objects. Removing a value restores the next valid source rather than writing a visually similar literal.

#### States and Edge Conditions

- Empty: explain the first useful action and provide it directly; do not display a dead panel.
- Loading or computing: retain last valid content when safe, show bounded progress, and allow cancellation for user-initiated work.
- Mixed or partially applicable: identify the affected subset and preserve differences until the user commits a unifying value.
- Invalid: retain the user’s draft separately, state the violated rule, and offer specific repair without replacing committed data.
- Missing dependency: preserve the reference and editable intent, use a defined fallback, and provide locate, replace, or detach actions.
- Read-only or denied: explain the governing policy and keep inspection, copy, and export available where permitted.
- Offline or service unavailable: keep local authoring operational; queue only idempotent connected operations and display their state.
- Large selection or project: virtualize and batch presentation while keeping the mutation atomic and cancelable.

### 4.2 Selection engine

Module code  0402

Defines hit testing, single and multi-selection, containment, cycling, marquee selection, and selection persistence.

#### Scope and Outcomes

- Primary objects: selection set, primary selection, hit target, selection scope, marquee, ancestor.
- Primary user outcomes: select visible objects; drill into containers; add or remove selection; select by layer.
- Critical invariant: selection is deterministic for the same scene; locked or hidden nodes follow explicit policies.
- The module includes authoring UI, model semantics, persistence, history, preview/export behavior, accessibility, diagnostics, migrations, and verification unless explicitly excluded.
- The module excludes connected-service implementation details that are not needed for local authoring; those are handled behind adapters and permission boundaries.
#### Behavioral Model

The model for selection engine is authoritative and UI-independent. Editing uses a draft → validate → preview → commit sequence. A commit creates one transaction with an operation name, actor, timestamp, affected stable identifiers, and an inverse or restoration strategy. Background work consumes immutable snapshots and returns results tagged with the originating revision; stale results are ignored.

All controls show whether a value is authored, inherited, calculated, unavailable, or mixed. When multiple selections are involved, the system computes the applicable subset before preview. It must not silently coerce incompatible objects. Removing a value restores the next valid source rather than writing a visually similar literal.

#### States and Edge Conditions

- Empty: explain the first useful action and provide it directly; do not display a dead panel.
- Loading or computing: retain last valid content when safe, show bounded progress, and allow cancellation for user-initiated work.
- Mixed or partially applicable: identify the affected subset and preserve differences until the user commits a unifying value.
- Invalid: retain the user’s draft separately, state the violated rule, and offer specific repair without replacing committed data.
- Missing dependency: preserve the reference and editable intent, use a defined fallback, and provide locate, replace, or detach actions.
- Read-only or denied: explain the governing policy and keep inspection, copy, and export available where permitted.
- Offline or service unavailable: keep local authoring operational; queue only idempotent connected operations and display their state.
- Large selection or project: virtualize and batch presentation while keeping the mutation atomic and cancelable.

### 4.4 Snapping, guides, rulers, and measurement

Module code  0404

Defines candidate generation, priority, thresholds, smart guides, distances, persistent guides, and measurement overlays.

#### Scope and Outcomes

- Primary objects: snap candidate, guide, ruler, distance, threshold, alignment line.
- Primary user outcomes: snap to edges and centers; add guides; measure gaps; temporarily suppress snapping.
- Critical invariant: snapping is stable and non-jittery; winning candidates are visibly explained.
- The module includes authoring UI, model semantics, persistence, history, preview/export behavior, accessibility, diagnostics, migrations, and verification unless explicitly excluded.
- The module excludes connected-service implementation details that are not needed for local authoring; those are handled behind adapters and permission boundaries.
#### Behavioral Model

The model for snapping, guides, rulers, and measurement is authoritative and UI-independent. Editing uses a draft → validate → preview → commit sequence. A commit creates one transaction with an operation name, actor, timestamp, affected stable identifiers, and an inverse or restoration strategy. Background work consumes immutable snapshots and returns results tagged with the originating revision; stale results are ignored.

All controls show whether a value is authored, inherited, calculated, unavailable, or mixed. When multiple selections are involved, the system computes the applicable subset before preview. It must not silently coerce incompatible objects. Removing a value restores the next valid source rather than writing a visually similar literal.

#### States and Edge Conditions

- Empty: explain the first useful action and provide it directly; do not display a dead panel.
- Loading or computing: retain last valid content when safe, show bounded progress, and allow cancellation for user-initiated work.
- Mixed or partially applicable: identify the affected subset and preserve differences until the user commits a unifying value.
- Invalid: retain the user’s draft separately, state the violated rule, and offer specific repair without replacing committed data.
- Missing dependency: preserve the reference and editable intent, use a defined fallback, and provide locate, replace, or detach actions.
- Read-only or denied: explain the governing policy and keep inspection, copy, and export available where permitted.
- Offline or service unavailable: keep local authoring operational; queue only idempotent connected operations and display their state.
- Large selection or project: virtualize and batch presentation while keeping the mutation atomic and cancelable.

The authoritative state is expressed through snap candidate; UI convenience state cannot become a second source of truth.

### 4.6 Inline text editing on canvas

Module code  0406

Defines activation, selection handoff, caret behavior, text editing overlays, IME, rich ranges, and exit behavior.

#### Scope and Outcomes

- Primary objects: text node, caret, range, composition, paragraph, inline style.
- Primary user outcomes: enter and exit editing; type with IME; style a range; select text versus node.
- Critical invariant: text input is never interpreted as a canvas shortcut; composition is not split by autosave or undo.
- The module includes authoring UI, model semantics, persistence, history, preview/export behavior, accessibility, diagnostics, migrations, and verification unless explicitly excluded.
- The module excludes connected-service implementation details that are not needed for local authoring; those are handled behind adapters and permission boundaries.
#### Behavioral Model

The model for inline text editing on canvas is authoritative and UI-independent. Editing uses a draft → validate → preview → commit sequence. A commit creates one transaction with an operation name, actor, timestamp, affected stable identifiers, and an inverse or restoration strategy. Background work consumes immutable snapshots and returns results tagged with the originating revision; stale results are ignored.

All controls show whether a value is authored, inherited, calculated, unavailable, or mixed. When multiple selections are involved, the system computes the applicable subset before preview. It must not silently coerce incompatible objects. Removing a value restores the next valid source rather than writing a visually similar literal.

#### States and Edge Conditions

- Empty: explain the first useful action and provide it directly; do not display a dead panel.
- Loading or computing: retain last valid content when safe, show bounded progress, and allow cancellation for user-initiated work.
- Mixed or partially applicable: identify the affected subset and preserve differences until the user commits a unifying value.
- Invalid: retain the user’s draft separately, state the violated rule, and offer specific repair without replacing committed data.
- Missing dependency: preserve the reference and editable intent, use a defined fallback, and provide locate, replace, or detach actions.
- Read-only or denied: explain the governing policy and keep inspection, copy, and export available where permitted.
- Offline or service unavailable: keep local authoring operational; queue only idempotent connected operations and display their state.
- Large selection or project: virtualize and batch presentation while keeping the mutation atomic and cancelable.

### 4.8 Drag and drop

Module code  0408

Defines internal and external drags, payload negotiation, drop targeting, previews, autoscroll, and cancellation.

#### Scope and Outcomes

- Primary objects: drag session, payload, drop zone, insertion indicator, operation type.
- Primary user outcomes: reorder layers; place assets; nest nodes; import files; drag across panels.
- Critical invariant: the preview matches the eventual insertion point; rejected drops communicate the constraint.
- The module includes authoring UI, model semantics, persistence, history, preview/export behavior, accessibility, diagnostics, migrations, and verification unless explicitly excluded.
- The module excludes connected-service implementation details that are not needed for local authoring; those are handled behind adapters and permission boundaries.
#### Behavioral Model

The model for drag and drop is authoritative and UI-independent. Editing uses a draft → validate → preview → commit sequence. A commit creates one transaction with an operation name, actor, timestamp, affected stable identifiers, and an inverse or restoration strategy. Background work consumes immutable snapshots and returns results tagged with the originating revision; stale results are ignored.

All controls show whether a value is authored, inherited, calculated, unavailable, or mixed. When multiple selections are involved, the system computes the applicable subset before preview. It must not silently coerce incompatible objects. Removing a value restores the next valid source rather than writing a visually similar literal.

#### States and Edge Conditions

- Empty: explain the first useful action and provide it directly; do not display a dead panel.
- Loading or computing: retain last valid content when safe, show bounded progress, and allow cancellation for user-initiated work.
- Mixed or partially applicable: identify the affected subset and preserve differences until the user commits a unifying value.
- Invalid: retain the user’s draft separately, state the violated rule, and offer specific repair without replacing committed data.
- Missing dependency: preserve the reference and editable intent, use a defined fallback, and provide locate, replace, or detach actions.
- Read-only or denied: explain the governing policy and keep inspection, copy, and export available where permitted.
- Offline or service unavailable: keep local authoring operational; queue only idempotent connected operations and display their state.
- Large selection or project: virtualize and batch presentation while keeping the mutation atomic and cancelable.

## V. Layout and Styling

This part is normative. Module introductions establish scope; numbered requirements define verifiable obligations. Cross-cutting requirements in Quality Attributes and Testing apply even when not repeated in a module.

### 5.1 Layout engine foundations

Module code  0501

Defines boxes, intrinsic sizes, containing blocks, formatting contexts, constraints, and deterministic layout.

Implementation note (2026-07-21): `SF-AUTHORING-002` verifies a bounded production engine subset for `SF-0501-001` through `SF-0501-008`: headless versioned stable-ID snapshots, fixed/intrinsic/fill sizing, min/max, padding, gap, start/center/end/stretch alignment, horizontal/vertical stacks, nesting, visible/clip overflow, responsive widths, typed validation, cancellation/stale-result rejection, deterministic digests, and isolated browser-oracle parity. The normative requirements remain Partial overall because canonical authored property commands/persistence, inspector and accessibility UI, renderer integration, production text shaping, incremental layout, preview/export UI, and owner-approved hardware budgets are not part of this slice.

#### Scope and Outcomes

- Primary objects: layout box, containing block, intrinsic size, constraint, fragment, baseline.
- Primary user outcomes: compute size and position; resolve intrinsic content; relayout after property change.
- Critical invariant: identical inputs produce identical geometry; invalid constraints yield diagnostics rather than undefined output.
- The module includes authoring UI, model semantics, persistence, history, preview/export behavior, accessibility, diagnostics, migrations, and verification unless explicitly excluded.
- The module excludes connected-service implementation details that are not needed for local authoring; those are handled behind adapters and permission boundaries.
#### Behavioral Model

The model for layout engine foundations is authoritative and UI-independent. Editing uses a draft → validate → preview → commit sequence. A commit creates one transaction with an operation name, actor, timestamp, affected stable identifiers, and an inverse or restoration strategy. Background work consumes immutable snapshots and returns results tagged with the originating revision; stale results are ignored.

All controls show whether a value is authored, inherited, calculated, unavailable, or mixed. When multiple selections are involved, the system computes the applicable subset before preview. It must not silently coerce incompatible objects. Removing a value restores the next valid source rather than writing a visually similar literal.

#### States and Edge Conditions

- Empty: explain the first useful action and provide it directly; do not display a dead panel.
- Loading or computing: retain last valid content when safe, show bounded progress, and allow cancellation for user-initiated work.
- Mixed or partially applicable: identify the affected subset and preserve differences until the user commits a unifying value.
- Invalid: retain the user’s draft separately, state the violated rule, and offer specific repair without replacing committed data.
- Missing dependency: preserve the reference and editable intent, use a defined fallback, and provide locate, replace, or detach actions.
- Read-only or denied: explain the governing policy and keep inspection, copy, and export available where permitted.
- Offline or service unavailable: keep local authoring operational; queue only idempotent connected operations and display their state.
- Large selection or project: virtualize and batch presentation while keeping the mutation atomic and cancelable.

The authoritative state is expressed through layout box; UI convenience state cannot become a second source of truth.

- Given valid layout box state, performing the operation through pointer, keyboard, menu, or an applicable automation API commits one equivalent transaction and produces the specified result.
- Cancel, Escape, validation failure, permission denial, or subsystem interruption leaves the last committed document unchanged and provides a specific recovery action.
- Save, close, reopen, undo, redo, duplication, and version comparison preserve the result and its identity; identical inputs produce identical geometry.
- Accessibility labels, focus order, announcements, and reduced-motion behavior expose the same capability without requiring pixel-precise pointer input.
- Diagnostics include requirement ID SF-0501-001, operation type, sanitized object identifiers, duration, and failure category; content values and secrets are excluded by default.
Verification  Unit tests cover resolution and invalid inputs; integration tests cover transaction and persistence boundaries; UI tests cover the primary journey and cancellation; exploratory QA covers scale, localization, accessibility, and recovery. ### 5.3 Grid layout

Module code  0503

Defines explicit and implicit tracks, lines, areas, minmax, auto-placement, spanning, gaps, and responsive changes.

#### Scope and Outcomes

- Primary objects: grid, track, line, area, span, auto-flow, minmax.
- Primary user outcomes: define tracks; place and span children; name areas; inspect implicit tracks.
- Critical invariant: placements remain valid as tracks change or produce actionable repair guidance.
- The module includes authoring UI, model semantics, persistence, history, preview/export behavior, accessibility, diagnostics, migrations, and verification unless explicitly excluded.
- The module excludes connected-service implementation details that are not needed for local authoring; those are handled behind adapters and permission boundaries.
#### Behavioral Model

The model for grid layout is authoritative and UI-independent. Editing uses a draft → validate → preview → commit sequence. A commit creates one transaction with an operation name, actor, timestamp, affected stable identifiers, and an inverse or restoration strategy. Background work consumes immutable snapshots and returns results tagged with the originating revision; stale results are ignored.

All controls show whether a value is authored, inherited, calculated, unavailable, or mixed. When multiple selections are involved, the system computes the applicable subset before preview. It must not silently coerce incompatible objects. Removing a value restores the next valid source rather than writing a visually similar literal.

#### States and Edge Conditions

- Empty: explain the first useful action and provide it directly; do not display a dead panel.
- Loading or computing: retain last valid content when safe, show bounded progress, and allow cancellation for user-initiated work.
- Mixed or partially applicable: identify the affected subset and preserve differences until the user commits a unifying value.
- Invalid: retain the user’s draft separately, state the violated rule, and offer specific repair without replacing committed data.
- Missing dependency: preserve the reference and editable intent, use a defined fallback, and provide locate, replace, or detach actions.
- Read-only or denied: explain the governing policy and keep inspection, copy, and export available where permitted.
- Offline or service unavailable: keep local authoring operational; queue only idempotent connected operations and display their state.
- Large selection or project: virtualize and batch presentation while keeping the mutation atomic and cancelable.

### 5.5 Sizing, constraints, and aspect ratios

Module code  0505

Defines fixed, hug, fill, min/max, viewport-relative, percentage, and aspect-ratio sizing.

#### Scope and Outcomes

- Primary objects: size mode, min, max, percentage, viewport unit, aspect ratio.
- Primary user outcomes: switch sizing modes; resolve constraints; preserve ratios; expose over-constraint.
- Critical invariant: resolution order is documented and inspectable; impossible ranges are rejected or normalized.
- The module includes authoring UI, model semantics, persistence, history, preview/export behavior, accessibility, diagnostics, migrations, and verification unless explicitly excluded.
- The module excludes connected-service implementation details that are not needed for local authoring; those are handled behind adapters and permission boundaries.
#### Behavioral Model

The model for sizing, constraints, and aspect ratios is authoritative and UI-independent. Editing uses a draft → validate → preview → commit sequence. A commit creates one transaction with an operation name, actor, timestamp, affected stable identifiers, and an inverse or restoration strategy. Background work consumes immutable snapshots and returns results tagged with the originating revision; stale results are ignored.

All controls show whether a value is authored, inherited, calculated, unavailable, or mixed. When multiple selections are involved, the system computes the applicable subset before preview. It must not silently coerce incompatible objects. Removing a value restores the next valid source rather than writing a visually similar literal.

#### States and Edge Conditions

- Empty: explain the first useful action and provide it directly; do not display a dead panel.
- Loading or computing: retain last valid content when safe, show bounded progress, and allow cancellation for user-initiated work.
- Mixed or partially applicable: identify the affected subset and preserve differences until the user commits a unifying value.
- Invalid: retain the user’s draft separately, state the violated rule, and offer specific repair without replacing committed data.
- Missing dependency: preserve the reference and editable intent, use a defined fallback, and provide locate, replace, or detach actions.
- Read-only or denied: explain the governing policy and keep inspection, copy, and export available where permitted.
- Offline or service unavailable: keep local authoring operational; queue only idempotent connected operations and display their state.
- Large selection or project: virtualize and batch presentation while keeping the mutation atomic and cancelable.

### 5.7 Typography system

Module code  0507

Defines font families, variable axes, weights, line height, letter spacing, paragraph settings, lists, links, and fallback.

#### Scope and Outcomes

- Primary objects: font face, family, axis, text style, paragraph, glyph, fallback chain.
- Primary user outcomes: choose fonts; apply type styles; adjust paragraphs; load local and web fonts.
- Critical invariant: missing fonts degrade predictably and are diagnosed; editing and export shape text consistently.
- The module includes authoring UI, model semantics, persistence, history, preview/export behavior, accessibility, diagnostics, migrations, and verification unless explicitly excluded.
- The module excludes connected-service implementation details that are not needed for local authoring; those are handled behind adapters and permission boundaries.
#### Behavioral Model

The model for typography system is authoritative and UI-independent. Editing uses a draft → validate → preview → commit sequence. A commit creates one transaction with an operation name, actor, timestamp, affected stable identifiers, and an inverse or restoration strategy. Background work consumes immutable snapshots and returns results tagged with the originating revision; stale results are ignored.

All controls show whether a value is authored, inherited, calculated, unavailable, or mixed. When multiple selections are involved, the system computes the applicable subset before preview. It must not silently coerce incompatible objects. Removing a value restores the next valid source rather than writing a visually similar literal.

#### States and Edge Conditions

- Empty: explain the first useful action and provide it directly; do not display a dead panel.
- Loading or computing: retain last valid content when safe, show bounded progress, and allow cancellation for user-initiated work.
- Mixed or partially applicable: identify the affected subset and preserve differences until the user commits a unifying value.
- Invalid: retain the user’s draft separately, state the violated rule, and offer specific repair without replacing committed data.
- Missing dependency: preserve the reference and editable intent, use a defined fallback, and provide locate, replace, or detach actions.
- Read-only or denied: explain the governing policy and keep inspection, copy, and export available where permitted.
- Offline or service unavailable: keep local authoring operational; queue only idempotent connected operations and display their state.
- Large selection or project: virtualize and batch presentation while keeping the mutation atomic and cancelable.

### 5.9 Design tokens and variables

Module code  0509

Defines typed tokens, collections, modes, aliases, scoping, fallback, documentation, and export mapping.

#### Scope and Outcomes

- Primary objects: token, collection, mode, alias, scope, fallback, semantic name.
- Primary user outcomes: create and organize tokens; switch themes; alias values; publish token outputs.
- Critical invariant: cycles are impossible or reported; deleting a token requires safe reference handling.
- The module includes authoring UI, model semantics, persistence, history, preview/export behavior, accessibility, diagnostics, migrations, and verification unless explicitly excluded.
- The module excludes connected-service implementation details that are not needed for local authoring; those are handled behind adapters and permission boundaries.
#### Behavioral Model

The model for design tokens and variables is authoritative and UI-independent. Editing uses a draft → validate → preview → commit sequence. A commit creates one transaction with an operation name, actor, timestamp, affected stable identifiers, and an inverse or restoration strategy. Background work consumes immutable snapshots and returns results tagged with the originating revision; stale results are ignored.

All controls show whether a value is authored, inherited, calculated, unavailable, or mixed. When multiple selections are involved, the system computes the applicable subset before preview. It must not silently coerce incompatible objects. Removing a value restores the next valid source rather than writing a visually similar literal.

#### States and Edge Conditions

- Empty: explain the first useful action and provide it directly; do not display a dead panel.
- Loading or computing: retain last valid content when safe, show bounded progress, and allow cancellation for user-initiated work.
- Mixed or partially applicable: identify the affected subset and preserve differences until the user commits a unifying value.
- Invalid: retain the user’s draft separately, state the violated rule, and offer specific repair without replacing committed data.
- Missing dependency: preserve the reference and editable intent, use a defined fallback, and provide locate, replace, or detach actions.
- Read-only or denied: explain the governing policy and keep inspection, copy, and export available where permitted.
- Offline or service unavailable: keep local authoring operational; queue only idempotent connected operations and display their state.
- Large selection or project: virtualize and batch presentation while keeping the mutation atomic and cancelable.
#### Normative Requirements

##### SF-0509-001 — Authoritative state

Requirement  The system MUST represent this capability in the canonical project model with stable identity, explicit defaults, typed validation, and versioned serialization. The serialized representation MUST distinguish omitted, defaulted, and explicitly authored values for token.

Rationale  This requirement exists so that create and organize tokens remains predictable when the project grows, is reopened, is exported, or is operated through an accessibility path. The authoritative state is expressed through token; UI convenience state cannot become a second source of truth.

Acceptance criteria  The following observations are required:

- Given valid token state, performing the operation through pointer, keyboard, menu, or an applicable automation API commits one equivalent transaction and produces the specified result.
- Cancel, Escape, validation failure, permission denial, or subsystem interruption leaves the last committed document unchanged and provides a specific recovery action.
- Save, close, reopen, undo, redo, duplication, and version comparison preserve the result and its identity; cycles are impossible or reported.
- Accessibility labels, focus order, announcements, and reduced-motion behavior expose the same capability without requiring pixel-precise pointer input.
- Diagnostics include requirement ID SF-0509-001, operation type, sanitized object identifiers, duration, and failure category; content values and secrets are excluded by default.
Verification  Unit tests cover resolution and invalid inputs; integration tests cover transaction and persistence boundaries; UI tests cover the primary journey and cancellation; exploratory QA covers scale, localization, accessibility, and recovery. Requirement owner records evidence in the traceability index.

Priority / milestone  MUST. Release blocking for the first milestone in which this module is enabled; later refinements may be separately scoped only when the mandatory path remains complete.

All controls show whether a value is authored, inherited, calculated, unavailable, or mixed. When multiple selections are involved, the system computes the applicable subset before preview. It must not silently coerce incompatible objects. Removing a value restores the next valid source rather than writing a visually similar literal.

#### States and Edge Conditions

- Empty: explain the first useful action and provide it directly; do not display a dead panel.
- Loading or computing: retain last valid content when safe, show bounded progress, and allow cancellation for user-initiated work.
- Mixed or partially applicable: identify the affected subset and preserve differences until the user commits a unifying value.
- Invalid: retain the user’s draft separately, state the violated rule, and offer specific repair without replacing committed data.
- Missing dependency: preserve the reference and editable intent, use a defined fallback, and provide locate, replace, or detach actions.
- Read-only or denied: explain the governing policy and keep inspection, copy, and export available where permitted.
- Offline or service unavailable: keep local authoring operational; queue only idempotent connected operations and display their state.
- Large selection or project: virtualize and batch presentation while keeping the mutation atomic and cancelable.

Acceptance criteria  The following observations are required:

- Cancel, Escape, validation failure, permission denial, or subsystem interruption leaves the last committed document unchanged and provides a specific recovery action.
- Save, close, reopen, undo, redo, duplication, and version comparison preserve the result and its identity; keyboard focus remains visible.
- Accessibility labels, focus order, announcements, and reduced-motion behavior expose the same capability without requiring pixel-precise pointer input.
- Diagnostics include requirement ID SF-0511-001, operation type, sanitized object identifiers, duration, and failure category; content values and secrets are excluded by default.
Verification  Unit tests cover resolution and invalid inputs; integration tests cover transaction and persistence boundaries; UI tests cover the primary journey and cancellation; exploratory QA covers scale, localization, accessibility, and recovery. ### 6.1 Breakpoint model and cascade

Module code  0601

Defines default-first or breakpoint-first semantics, breakpoint creation, ranges, inheritance, conflicts, and ordering.

#### Scope and Outcomes

- Primary objects: breakpoint, range, base value, override, cascade, conflict.
- Primary user outcomes: add and edit breakpoints; author overrides; inspect inherited values; remove overrides.

### 6.3 Adaptive visibility and content

Module code  0603

Defines conditional visibility, responsive source selection, content substitution policy, and accessibility implications.

#### Scope and Outcomes

- Primary objects: visibility rule, conditional content, source set, alternate asset.
- Primary user outcomes: hide or swap content by range; preview conditions; diagnose unreachable content.
- Critical invariant: hidden content has explicit DOM and accessibility behavior; critical information is not silently lost.
- The module includes authoring UI, model semantics, persistence, history, preview/export behavior, accessibility, diagnostics, migrations, and verification unless explicitly excluded.
- The module excludes connected-service implementation details that are not needed for local authoring; those are handled behind adapters and permission boundaries.
#### Behavioral Model

The model for adaptive visibility and content is authoritative and UI-independent. Editing uses a draft → validate → preview → commit sequence. A commit creates one transaction with an operation name, actor, timestamp, affected stable identifiers, and an inverse or restoration strategy. Background work consumes immutable snapshots and returns results tagged with the originating revision; stale results are ignored.

All controls show whether a value is authored, inherited, calculated, unavailable, or mixed. When multiple selections are involved, the system computes the applicable subset before preview. It must not silently coerce incompatible objects. Removing a value restores the next valid source rather than writing a visually similar literal.

#### States and Edge Conditions

- Empty: explain the first useful action and provide it directly; do not display a dead panel.
- Loading or computing: retain last valid content when safe, show bounded progress, and allow cancellation for user-initiated work.
- Mixed or partially applicable: identify the affected subset and preserve differences until the user commits a unifying value.
- Invalid: retain the user’s draft separately, state the violated rule, and offer specific repair without replacing committed data.
- Missing dependency: preserve the reference and editable intent, use a defined fallback, and provide locate, replace, or detach actions.
- Read-only or denied: explain the governing policy and keep inspection, copy, and export available where permitted.
- Offline or service unavailable: keep local authoring operational; queue only idempotent connected operations and display their state.
- Large selection or project: virtualize and batch presentation while keeping the mutation atomic and cancelable.

### 6.5 Container queries and component responsiveness

Module code  0605

Defines query containers, named contexts, thresholds, style variants, nested evaluation, and export compatibility.

#### Scope and Outcomes

- Primary objects: query container, container size, threshold, responsive variant.
- Primary user outcomes: make components adapt to their container; preview nested contexts; inspect matches.
- Critical invariant: container dependencies are cycle-safe; unsupported targets receive a defined fallback.
- The module includes authoring UI, model semantics, persistence, history, preview/export behavior, accessibility, diagnostics, migrations, and verification unless explicitly excluded.
- The module excludes connected-service implementation details that are not needed for local authoring; those are handled behind adapters and permission boundaries.
#### Behavioral Model

The model for container queries and component responsiveness is authoritative and UI-independent. Editing uses a draft → validate → preview → commit sequence. A commit creates one transaction with an operation name, actor, timestamp, affected stable identifiers, and an inverse or restoration strategy. Background work consumes immutable snapshots and returns results tagged with the originating revision; stale results are ignored.

All controls show whether a value is authored, inherited, calculated, unavailable, or mixed. When multiple selections are involved, the system computes the applicable subset before preview. It must not silently coerce incompatible objects. Removing a value restores the next valid source rather than writing a visually similar literal.

#### States and Edge Conditions

- Empty: explain the first useful action and provide it directly; do not display a dead panel.
- Loading or computing: retain last valid content when safe, show bounded progress, and allow cancellation for user-initiated work.
- Mixed or partially applicable: identify the affected subset and preserve differences until the user commits a unifying value.
- Invalid: retain the user’s draft separately, state the violated rule, and offer specific repair without replacing committed data.
- Missing dependency: preserve the reference and editable intent, use a defined fallback, and provide locate, replace, or detach actions.
- Read-only or denied: explain the governing policy and keep inspection, copy, and export available where permitted.
- Offline or service unavailable: keep local authoring operational; queue only idempotent connected operations and display their state.
- Large selection or project: virtualize and batch presentation while keeping the mutation atomic and cancelable.

## VII. Inspector and Authoring Controls

This part is normative. Module introductions establish scope; numbered requirements define verifiable obligations. Cross-cutting requirements in Quality Attributes and Testing apply even when not repeated in a module.

### 7.1 Inspector architecture and sections

Module code  0701

Defines section registration, ordering, disclosure, pinned controls, context switching, and search.

#### Scope and Outcomes

- Primary objects: inspector section, property editor, disclosure state, context, pin.
- Primary user outcomes: inspect one or many objects; search properties; pin frequent controls; reset sections.
- Critical invariant: controls reflect the primary selection and mixed values without destroying differences.
- The module includes authoring UI, model semantics, persistence, history, preview/export behavior, accessibility, diagnostics, migrations, and verification unless explicitly excluded.
- The module excludes connected-service implementation details that are not needed for local authoring; those are handled behind adapters and permission boundaries.
#### Behavioral Model

The model for inspector architecture and sections is authoritative and UI-independent. Editing uses a draft → validate → preview → commit sequence. A commit creates one transaction with an operation name, actor, timestamp, affected stable identifiers, and an inverse or restoration strategy. Background work consumes immutable snapshots and returns results tagged with the originating revision; stale results are ignored.

All controls show whether a value is authored, inherited, calculated, unavailable, or mixed. When multiple selections are involved, the system computes the applicable subset before preview. It must not silently coerce incompatible objects. Removing a value restores the next valid source rather than writing a visually similar literal.

#### States and Edge Conditions

- Empty: explain the first useful action and provide it directly; do not display a dead panel.
- Loading or computing: retain last valid content when safe, show bounded progress, and allow cancellation for user-initiated work.
- Mixed or partially applicable: identify the affected subset and preserve differences until the user commits a unifying value.
- Invalid: retain the user’s draft separately, state the violated rule, and offer specific repair without replacing committed data.
- Missing dependency: preserve the reference and editable intent, use a defined fallback, and provide locate, replace, or detach actions.
- Read-only or denied: explain the governing policy and keep inspection, copy, and export available where permitted.
- Offline or service unavailable: keep local authoring operational; queue only idempotent connected operations and display their state.
- Large selection or project: virtualize and batch presentation while keeping the mutation atomic and cancelable.
