## XV. Native macOS Platform

This part is normative. Module introductions establish scope; numbered requirements define verifiable obligations. Cross-cutting requirements in Quality Attributes and Testing apply even when not repeated in a module.

### 15.1 macOS application architecture

Module code  1501

Defines Swift and SwiftUI/AppKit boundaries, document architecture, concurrency, process isolation, and framework policy.

#### Scope and Outcomes

- Primary objects: app process, document controller, scene, model actor, worker process, XPC boundary.
- Primary user outcomes: open windows and documents; run heavy tasks off main thread; isolate risky work.
- Critical invariant: UI state is main-actor safe; disk and compilation work cannot block interaction budgets.
- The module includes authoring UI, model semantics, persistence, history, preview/export behavior, accessibility, diagnostics, migrations, and verification unless explicitly excluded.
- The module excludes connected-service implementation details that are not needed for local authoring; those are handled behind adapters and permission boundaries.
#### Behavioral Model

The model for macos application architecture is authoritative and UI-independent. Editing uses a draft → validate → preview → commit sequence. A commit creates one transaction with an operation name, actor, timestamp, affected stable identifiers, and an inverse or restoration strategy. Background work consumes immutable snapshots and returns results tagged with the originating revision; stale results are ignored.

All controls show whether a value is authored, inherited, calculated, unavailable, or mixed. When multiple selections are involved, the system computes the applicable subset before preview. It must not silently coerce incompatible objects. Removing a value restores the next valid source rather than writing a visually similar literal.

#### States and Edge Conditions

- Empty: explain the first useful action and provide it directly; do not display a dead panel.
- Loading or computing: retain last valid content when safe, show bounded progress, and allow cancellation for user-initiated work.
- Mixed or partially applicable: identify the affected subset and preserve differences until the user commits a unifying value.
- Invalid: retain the user’s draft separately, state the violated rule, and offer specific repair without replacing committed data.
- Missing dependency: preserve the reference and editable intent, use a defined fallback, and provide locate, replace, or detach actions.
- Read-only or denied: explain the governing policy and keep inspection, copy, and export available where permitted.
- Offline or service unavailable: keep local authoring operational; queue only idempotent connected operations and display their state.
- Large selection or project: virtualize and batch presentation while keeping the mutation atomic and cancelable.

### 15.3 macOS input, menus, and services

Module code  1503

Defines pointer, trackpad, keyboard, pressure policy, contextual menus, drag services, sharing, and system services.

#### Scope and Outcomes

- Primary objects: event, gesture, key equivalent, contextual menu, service, pasteboard.
- Primary user outcomes: use trackpad gestures; invoke native menus; share exports; integrate pasteboard.
- Critical invariant: system conventions win unless a documented canvas interaction requires deviation.
- The module includes authoring UI, model semantics, persistence, history, preview/export behavior, accessibility, diagnostics, migrations, and verification unless explicitly excluded.
- The module excludes connected-service implementation details that are not needed for local authoring; those are handled behind adapters and permission boundaries.
#### Behavioral Model

The model for macos input, menus, and services is authoritative and UI-independent. Editing uses a draft → validate → preview → commit sequence. A commit creates one transaction with an operation name, actor, timestamp, affected stable identifiers, and an inverse or restoration strategy. Background work consumes immutable snapshots and returns results tagged with the originating revision; stale results are ignored.

All controls show whether a value is authored, inherited, calculated, unavailable, or mixed. When multiple selections are involved, the system computes the applicable subset before preview. It must not silently coerce incompatible objects. Removing a value restores the next valid source rather than writing a visually similar literal.

#### States and Edge Conditions

- Empty: explain the first useful action and provide it directly; do not display a dead panel.
- Loading or computing: retain last valid content when safe, show bounded progress, and allow cancellation for user-initiated work.
- Mixed or partially applicable: identify the affected subset and preserve differences until the user commits a unifying value.
- Invalid: retain the user’s draft separately, state the violated rule, and offer specific repair without replacing committed data.
- Missing dependency: preserve the reference and editable intent, use a defined fallback, and provide locate, replace, or detach actions.
- Read-only or denied: explain the governing policy and keep inspection, copy, and export available where permitted.
- Offline or service unavailable: keep local authoring operational; queue only idempotent connected operations and display their state.
- Large selection or project: virtualize and batch presentation while keeping the mutation atomic and cancelable.

### 15.5 Accessibility on macOS

Module code  1505

Defines VoiceOver, Full Keyboard Access, Switch Control, reduce motion, contrast, focus, and accessibility tree.

#### Scope and Outcomes

- Primary objects: accessibility element, role, label, value, action, rotor, focus.
- Primary user outcomes: operate every command and inspector control without pointer; navigate canvas representation.
- Critical invariant: custom canvas controls expose equivalent semantic operations; focus never disappears.
- The module includes authoring UI, model semantics, persistence, history, preview/export behavior, accessibility, diagnostics, migrations, and verification unless explicitly excluded.
- The module excludes connected-service implementation details that are not needed for local authoring; those are handled behind adapters and permission boundaries.
#### Behavioral Model

The model for accessibility on macos is authoritative and UI-independent. Editing uses a draft → validate → preview → commit sequence. A commit creates one transaction with an operation name, actor, timestamp, affected stable identifiers, and an inverse or restoration strategy. Background work consumes immutable snapshots and returns results tagged with the originating revision; stale results are ignored.

All controls show whether a value is authored, inherited, calculated, unavailable, or mixed. When multiple selections are involved, the system computes the applicable subset before preview. It must not silently coerce incompatible objects. Removing a value restores the next valid source rather than writing a visually similar literal.

#### States and Edge Conditions

- Empty: explain the first useful action and provide it directly; do not display a dead panel.
- Loading or computing: retain last valid content when safe, show bounded progress, and allow cancellation for user-initiated work.
- Mixed or partially applicable: identify the affected subset and preserve differences until the user commits a unifying value.
- Invalid: retain the user’s draft separately, state the violated rule, and offer specific repair without replacing committed data.
- Missing dependency: preserve the reference and editable intent, use a defined fallback, and provide locate, replace, or detach actions.
- Read-only or denied: explain the governing policy and keep inspection, copy, and export available where permitted.
- Offline or service unavailable: keep local authoring operational; queue only idempotent connected operations and display their state.
- Large selection or project: virtualize and batch presentation while keeping the mutation atomic and cancelable.

### 15.7 Updates, signing, notarization, and distribution

Module code  1507

Defines build identities, hardened runtime, notarization, channels, update verification, migration, and rollback policy.

#### Scope and Outcomes

- Primary objects: code signature, notarization ticket, update feed, channel, migration.
- Primary user outcomes: ship stable and preview builds; verify updates; migrate; recover from failed launch.
- Critical invariant: only signed trusted updates install; project migrations preserve downgrade guidance and backups.
- The module includes authoring UI, model semantics, persistence, history, preview/export behavior, accessibility, diagnostics, migrations, and verification unless explicitly excluded.
- The module excludes connected-service implementation details that are not needed for local authoring; those are handled behind adapters and permission boundaries.
#### Behavioral Model

The model for updates, signing, notarization, and distribution is authoritative and UI-independent. Editing uses a draft → validate → preview → commit sequence. A commit creates one transaction with an operation name, actor, timestamp, affected stable identifiers, and an inverse or restoration strategy. Background work consumes immutable snapshots and returns results tagged with the originating revision; stale results are ignored.

All controls show whether a value is authored, inherited, calculated, unavailable, or mixed. When multiple selections are involved, the system computes the applicable subset before preview. It must not silently coerce incompatible objects. Removing a value restores the next valid source rather than writing a visually similar literal.

#### States and Edge Conditions

- Empty: explain the first useful action and provide it directly; do not display a dead panel.
- Loading or computing: retain last valid content when safe, show bounded progress, and allow cancellation for user-initiated work.
- Mixed or partially applicable: identify the affected subset and preserve differences until the user commits a unifying value.
- Invalid: retain the user’s draft separately, state the violated rule, and offer specific repair without replacing committed data.
- Missing dependency: preserve the reference and editable intent, use a defined fallback, and provide locate, replace, or detach actions.
- Read-only or denied: explain the governing policy and keep inspection, copy, and export available where permitted.
- Offline or service unavailable: keep local authoring operational; queue only idempotent connected operations and display their state.
- Large selection or project: virtualize and batch presentation while keeping the mutation atomic and cancelable.

### 16.2 Reliability and fault tolerance

Module code  1602

Defines failure domains, retries, timeouts, circuit breakers, degraded modes, crash recovery, and data integrity.

#### Scope and Outcomes

- Primary objects: failure domain, retry policy, timeout, degraded mode, health signal.
- Primary user outcomes: survive plugin, network, preview, and build failures; recover documents.
- Critical invariant: optional subsystem failures cannot corrupt the authoring model; retry never duplicates mutations.
- The module includes authoring UI, model semantics, persistence, history, preview/export behavior, accessibility, diagnostics, migrations, and verification unless explicitly excluded.
- The module excludes connected-service implementation details that are not needed for local authoring; those are handled behind adapters and permission boundaries.
#### Behavioral Model

The model for reliability and fault tolerance is authoritative and UI-independent. Editing uses a draft → validate → preview → commit sequence. A commit creates one transaction with an operation name, actor, timestamp, affected stable identifiers, and an inverse or restoration strategy. Background work consumes immutable snapshots and returns results tagged with the originating revision; stale results are ignored.

All controls show whether a value is authored, inherited, calculated, unavailable, or mixed. When multiple selections are involved, the system computes the applicable subset before preview. It must not silently coerce incompatible objects. Removing a value restores the next valid source rather than writing a visually similar literal.

#### States and Edge Conditions

- Empty: explain the first useful action and provide it directly; do not display a dead panel.
- Loading or computing: retain last valid content when safe, show bounded progress, and allow cancellation for user-initiated work.
- Mixed or partially applicable: identify the affected subset and preserve differences until the user commits a unifying value.
- Invalid: retain the user’s draft separately, state the violated rule, and offer specific repair without replacing committed data.
- Missing dependency: preserve the reference and editable intent, use a defined fallback, and provide locate, replace, or detach actions.
- Read-only or denied: explain the governing policy and keep inspection, copy, and export available where permitted.
- Offline or service unavailable: keep local authoring operational; queue only idempotent connected operations and display their state.
- Large selection or project: virtualize and batch presentation while keeping the mutation atomic and cancelable.

### 16.4 Privacy and data governance

Module code  1604

Defines data categories, purposes, minimization, consent, retention, deletion, export, regional policy, and vendor review.

#### Scope and Outcomes

- Primary objects: data category, purpose, consent, retention, deletion request, processor.
- Primary user outcomes: understand collection; opt out; export account data; delete connected data.
- Critical invariant: local project content stays local unless the user invokes a connected feature; telemetry excludes content by default.
- The module includes authoring UI, model semantics, persistence, history, preview/export behavior, accessibility, diagnostics, migrations, and verification unless explicitly excluded.
- The module excludes connected-service implementation details that are not needed for local authoring; those are handled behind adapters and permission boundaries.
#### Behavioral Model

The model for privacy and data governance is authoritative and UI-independent. Editing uses a draft → validate → preview → commit sequence. A commit creates one transaction with an operation name, actor, timestamp, affected stable identifiers, and an inverse or restoration strategy. Background work consumes immutable snapshots and returns results tagged with the originating revision; stale results are ignored.

All controls show whether a value is authored, inherited, calculated, unavailable, or mixed. When multiple selections are involved, the system computes the applicable subset before preview. It must not silently coerce incompatible objects. Removing a value restores the next valid source rather than writing a visually similar literal.

#### States and Edge Conditions

- Empty: explain the first useful action and provide it directly; do not display a dead panel.
- Loading or computing: retain last valid content when safe, show bounded progress, and allow cancellation for user-initiated work.
- Mixed or partially applicable: identify the affected subset and preserve differences until the user commits a unifying value.
- Invalid: retain the user’s draft separately, state the violated rule, and offer specific repair without replacing committed data.
- Missing dependency: preserve the reference and editable intent, use a defined fallback, and provide locate, replace, or detach actions.
- Read-only or denied: explain the governing policy and keep inspection, copy, and export available where permitted.
- Offline or service unavailable: keep local authoring operational; queue only idempotent connected operations and display their state.
- Large selection or project: virtualize and batch presentation while keeping the mutation atomic and cancelable.

### 16.6 Compatibility and browser policy

Module code  1606

Defines supported macOS versions, hardware, browsers for exported sites, feature detection, polyfills, and deprecation.

#### Scope and Outcomes

- Primary objects: platform target, browser target, capability, fallback, deprecation window.
- Primary user outcomes: run on supported Macs; export for target browsers; report incompatible features.
- Critical invariant: support matrices are versioned release inputs; removal follows a communicated policy.
- The module includes authoring UI, model semantics, persistence, history, preview/export behavior, accessibility, diagnostics, migrations, and verification unless explicitly excluded.
- The module excludes connected-service implementation details that are not needed for local authoring; those are handled behind adapters and permission boundaries.
#### Behavioral Model

The model for compatibility and browser policy is authoritative and UI-independent. Editing uses a draft → validate → preview → commit sequence. A commit creates one transaction with an operation name, actor, timestamp, affected stable identifiers, and an inverse or restoration strategy. Background work consumes immutable snapshots and returns results tagged with the originating revision; stale results are ignored.

All controls show whether a value is authored, inherited, calculated, unavailable, or mixed. When multiple selections are involved, the system computes the applicable subset before preview. It must not silently coerce incompatible objects. Removing a value restores the next valid source rather than writing a visually similar literal.

#### States and Edge Conditions

- Empty: explain the first useful action and provide it directly; do not display a dead panel.
- Loading or computing: retain last valid content when safe, show bounded progress, and allow cancellation for user-initiated work.
- Mixed or partially applicable: identify the affected subset and preserve differences until the user commits a unifying value.
- Invalid: retain the user’s draft separately, state the violated rule, and offer specific repair without replacing committed data.
- Missing dependency: preserve the reference and editable intent, use a defined fallback, and provide locate, replace, or detach actions.
- Read-only or denied: explain the governing policy and keep inspection, copy, and export available where permitted.
- Offline or service unavailable: keep local authoring operational; queue only idempotent connected operations and display their state.
- Large selection or project: virtualize and batch presentation while keeping the mutation atomic and cancelable.

☐ Save during active editing, forced termination, reopen, and migration preserve the last committed state.

☐ VoiceOver, Full Keyboard Access, high contrast, reduced motion, and 200% UI scaling complete the core flow.

☐ Preview and exported output either match authoring semantics or surface a documented compatibility finding.

☐ Diagnostics and support bundles remain useful with project-content inclusion disabled.

☐ Performance budgets pass for standard and large fixtures on named minimum and reference hardware.

## XVII. Testing and Verification

This part is normative. Module introductions establish scope; numbered requirements define verifiable obligations. Cross-cutting requirements in Quality Attributes and Testing apply even when not repeated in a module.

### 17.1 Testing strategy and pyramid

Module code  1701

Defines unit, property, integration, UI, snapshot, accessibility, performance, security, compatibility, and exploratory testing.

#### Scope and Outcomes

- Primary objects: test layer, fixture, oracle, coverage target, quarantine, flake.
- Primary user outcomes: choose the lowest effective layer; run suites; isolate flakes; report coverage.
- Critical invariant: critical requirements map to automated or documented manual verification; quarantines expire.
- The module includes authoring UI, model semantics, persistence, history, preview/export behavior, accessibility, diagnostics, migrations, and verification unless explicitly excluded.
- The module excludes connected-service implementation details that are not needed for local authoring; those are handled behind adapters and permission boundaries.
#### Behavioral Model

The model for testing strategy and pyramid is authoritative and UI-independent. Editing uses a draft → validate → preview → commit sequence. A commit creates one transaction with an operation name, actor, timestamp, affected stable identifiers, and an inverse or restoration strategy. Background work consumes immutable snapshots and returns results tagged with the originating revision; stale results are ignored.

All controls show whether a value is authored, inherited, calculated, unavailable, or mixed. When multiple selections are involved, the system computes the applicable subset before preview. It must not silently coerce incompatible objects. Removing a value restores the next valid source rather than writing a visually similar literal.

#### States and Edge Conditions

- Empty: explain the first useful action and provide it directly; do not display a dead panel.
- Loading or computing: retain last valid content when safe, show bounded progress, and allow cancellation for user-initiated work.
- Mixed or partially applicable: identify the affected subset and preserve differences until the user commits a unifying value.
- Invalid: retain the user’s draft separately, state the violated rule, and offer specific repair without replacing committed data.
- Missing dependency: preserve the reference and editable intent, use a defined fallback, and provide locate, replace, or detach actions.
- Read-only or denied: explain the governing policy and keep inspection, copy, and export available where permitted.
- Offline or service unavailable: keep local authoring operational; queue only idempotent connected operations and display their state.
- Large selection or project: virtualize and batch presentation while keeping the mutation atomic and cancelable.
#### Normative Requirements

##### SF-1701-001 — Authoritative state

Requirement  The system MUST represent this capability in the canonical project model with stable identity, explicit defaults, typed validation, and versioned serialization. The serialized representation MUST distinguish omitted, defaulted, and explicitly authored values for test layer.

Rationale  This requirement exists so that choose the lowest effective layer remains predictable when the project grows, is reopened, is exported, or is operated through an accessibility path. The authoritative state is expressed through test layer; UI convenience state cannot become a second source of truth.

Acceptance criteria  The following observations are required:

- Given valid test layer state, performing the operation through pointer, keyboard, menu, or an applicable automation API commits one equivalent transaction and produces the specified result.
- Cancel, Escape, validation failure, permission denial, or subsystem interruption leaves the last committed document unchanged and provides a specific recovery action.
- Save, close, reopen, undo, redo, duplication, and version comparison preserve the result and its identity; critical requirements map to automated or documented manual verification.
- Accessibility labels, focus order, announcements, and reduced-motion behavior expose the same capability without requiring pixel-precise pointer input.
- Diagnostics include requirement ID SF-1701-001, operation type, sanitized object identifiers, duration, and failure category; content values and secrets are excluded by default.
Verification  Unit tests cover resolution and invalid inputs; integration tests cover transaction and persistence boundaries; UI tests cover the primary journey and cancellation; exploratory QA covers scale, localization, accessibility, and recovery. Requirement owner records evidence in the traceability index.

Priority / milestone  MUST. Release blocking for the first milestone in which this module is enabled; later refinements may be separately scoped only when the mandatory path remains complete.

#### Behavioral Model

The model for canvas and interaction tests is authoritative and UI-independent. Editing uses a draft → validate → preview → commit sequence. A commit creates one transaction with an operation name, actor, timestamp, affected stable identifiers, and an inverse or restoration strategy. Background work consumes immutable snapshots and returns results tagged with the originating revision; stale results are ignored.

All controls show whether a value is authored, inherited, calculated, unavailable, or mixed. When multiple selections are involved, the system computes the applicable subset before preview. It must not silently coerce incompatible objects. Removing a value restores the next valid source rather than writing a visually similar literal.

#### States and Edge Conditions

- Empty: explain the first useful action and provide it directly; do not display a dead panel.
- Loading or computing: retain last valid content when safe, show bounded progress, and allow cancellation for user-initiated work.
- Mixed or partially applicable: identify the affected subset and preserve differences until the user commits a unifying value.
- Invalid: retain the user’s draft separately, state the violated rule, and offer specific repair without replacing committed data.
- Missing dependency: preserve the reference and editable intent, use a defined fallback, and provide locate, replace, or detach actions.
- Read-only or denied: explain the governing policy and keep inspection, copy, and export available where permitted.
- Offline or service unavailable: keep local authoring operational; queue only idempotent connected operations and display their state.
- Large selection or project: virtualize and batch presentation while keeping the mutation atomic and cancelable.

### 17.6 QA checklists and exploratory charters

Module code  1706

Defines structured manual review, risk-based charters, device and locale passes, evidence capture, and sign-off.

#### Scope and Outcomes

- Primary objects: checklist, charter, session, evidence, finding, sign-off.
- Primary user outcomes: perform feature, regression, accessibility, localization, and release candidate passes.
- Critical invariant: each pass records build, environment, scope, findings, and owner; skipped checks require an approved exception.
- The module includes authoring UI, model semantics, persistence, history, preview/export behavior, accessibility, diagnostics, migrations, and verification unless explicitly excluded.
- The module excludes connected-service implementation details that are not needed for local authoring; those are handled behind adapters and permission boundaries.
#### Behavioral Model

The model for qa checklists and exploratory charters is authoritative and UI-independent. Editing uses a draft → validate → preview → commit sequence. A commit creates one transaction with an operation name, actor, timestamp, affected stable identifiers, and an inverse or restoration strategy. Background work consumes immutable snapshots and returns results tagged with the originating revision; stale results are ignored.

All controls show whether a value is authored, inherited, calculated, unavailable, or mixed. When multiple selections are involved, the system computes the applicable subset before preview. It must not silently coerce incompatible objects. Removing a value restores the next valid source rather than writing a visually similar literal.

#### States and Edge Conditions

- Empty: explain the first useful action and provide it directly; do not display a dead panel.
- Loading or computing: retain last valid content when safe, show bounded progress, and allow cancellation for user-initiated work.
- Mixed or partially applicable: identify the affected subset and preserve differences until the user commits a unifying value.
- Invalid: retain the user’s draft separately, state the violated rule, and offer specific repair without replacing committed data.
- Missing dependency: preserve the reference and editable intent, use a defined fallback, and provide locate, replace, or detach actions.
- Read-only or denied: explain the governing policy and keep inspection, copy, and export available where permitted.
- Offline or service unavailable: keep local authoring operational; queue only idempotent connected operations and display their state.
- Large selection or project: virtualize and batch presentation while keeping the mutation atomic and cancelable.

## XVIII. Delivery and Operations

This part is normative. Module introductions establish scope; numbered requirements define verifiable obligations. Cross-cutting requirements in Quality Attributes and Testing apply even when not repeated in a module.

### 18.1 Engineering repository and module boundaries

Module code  1801

Defines source layout, packages, ownership, dependency direction, generated code, fixtures, and architectural enforcement.

#### Scope and Outcomes

- Primary objects: module, package, target, dependency, owner, generated source.
- Primary user outcomes: navigate and build subsystems independently; enforce allowed dependencies.
- Critical invariant: cycles across architecture layers fail CI; public APIs have owners and compatibility tests.
- The module includes authoring UI, model semantics, persistence, history, preview/export behavior, accessibility, diagnostics, migrations, and verification unless explicitly excluded.
- The module excludes connected-service implementation details that are not needed for local authoring; those are handled behind adapters and permission boundaries.
#### Behavioral Model

The model for engineering repository and module boundaries is authoritative and UI-independent. Editing uses a draft → validate → preview → commit sequence. A commit creates one transaction with an operation name, actor, timestamp, affected stable identifiers, and an inverse or restoration strategy. Background work consumes immutable snapshots and returns results tagged with the originating revision; stale results are ignored.

All controls show whether a value is authored, inherited, calculated, unavailable, or mixed. When multiple selections are involved, the system computes the applicable subset before preview. It must not silently coerce incompatible objects. Removing a value restores the next valid source rather than writing a visually similar literal.

#### States and Edge Conditions

- Empty: explain the first useful action and provide it directly; do not display a dead panel.
- Loading or computing: retain last valid content when safe, show bounded progress, and allow cancellation for user-initiated work.
- Mixed or partially applicable: identify the affected subset and preserve differences until the user commits a unifying value.
- Invalid: retain the user’s draft separately, state the violated rule, and offer specific repair without replacing committed data.
- Missing dependency: preserve the reference and editable intent, use a defined fallback, and provide locate, replace, or detach actions.
- Read-only or denied: explain the governing policy and keep inspection, copy, and export available where permitted.
- Offline or service unavailable: keep local authoring operational; queue only idempotent connected operations and display their state.
- Large selection or project: virtualize and batch presentation while keeping the mutation atomic and cancelable.

### 18.3 Feature flags and experimentation

Module code  1803

Defines flag types, scope, defaults, lifecycle, targeting, offline behavior, cleanup, and measurement.

#### Scope and Outcomes

- Primary objects: feature flag, variant, exposure, default, expiry, owner.
- Primary user outcomes: roll out safely; disable a failing feature; compare variants; remove expired flags.
- Critical invariant: flags do not fork persistent schema without migration policy; every flag has owner and removal date.
- The module includes authoring UI, model semantics, persistence, history, preview/export behavior, accessibility, diagnostics, migrations, and verification unless explicitly excluded.
- The module excludes connected-service implementation details that are not needed for local authoring; those are handled behind adapters and permission boundaries.
#### Behavioral Model

The model for feature flags and experimentation is authoritative and UI-independent. Editing uses a draft → validate → preview → commit sequence. A commit creates one transaction with an operation name, actor, timestamp, affected stable identifiers, and an inverse or restoration strategy. Background work consumes immutable snapshots and returns results tagged with the originating revision; stale results are ignored.

All controls show whether a value is authored, inherited, calculated, unavailable, or mixed. When multiple selections are involved, the system computes the applicable subset before preview. It must not silently coerce incompatible objects. Removing a value restores the next valid source rather than writing a visually similar literal.

#### States and Edge Conditions

- Empty: explain the first useful action and provide it directly; do not display a dead panel.
- Loading or computing: retain last valid content when safe, show bounded progress, and allow cancellation for user-initiated work.
- Mixed or partially applicable: identify the affected subset and preserve differences until the user commits a unifying value.
- Invalid: retain the user’s draft separately, state the violated rule, and offer specific repair without replacing committed data.
- Missing dependency: preserve the reference and editable intent, use a defined fallback, and provide locate, replace, or detach actions.
- Read-only or denied: explain the governing policy and keep inspection, copy, and export available where permitted.
- Offline or service unavailable: keep local authoring operational; queue only idempotent connected operations and display their state.
- Large selection or project: virtualize and batch presentation while keeping the mutation atomic and cancelable.

### 18.5 Support, incident, and feedback loop

Module code  1805

Defines feedback intake, support bundles, issue routing, incident command, status communication, postmortems, and prioritization.

#### Scope and Outcomes

- Primary objects: support case, incident, impact, commander, timeline, corrective action.
- Primary user outcomes: triage reports; diagnose with consented evidence; coordinate incidents; feed learning to roadmap.
- Critical invariant: support access is auditable; incident fixes add regression coverage and tracked corrective actions.
- The module includes authoring UI, model semantics, persistence, history, preview/export behavior, accessibility, diagnostics, migrations, and verification unless explicitly excluded.
- The module excludes connected-service implementation details that are not needed for local authoring; those are handled behind adapters and permission boundaries.
#### Behavioral Model

The model for support, incident, and feedback loop is authoritative and UI-independent. Editing uses a draft → validate → preview → commit sequence. A commit creates one transaction with an operation name, actor, timestamp, affected stable identifiers, and an inverse or restoration strategy. Background work consumes immutable snapshots and returns results tagged with the originating revision; stale results are ignored.

All controls show whether a value is authored, inherited, calculated, unavailable, or mixed. When multiple selections are involved, the system computes the applicable subset before preview. It must not silently coerce incompatible objects. Removing a value restores the next valid source rather than writing a visually similar literal.

#### States and Edge Conditions

- Empty: explain the first useful action and provide it directly; do not display a dead panel.
- Loading or computing: retain last valid content when safe, show bounded progress, and allow cancellation for user-initiated work.
- Mixed or partially applicable: identify the affected subset and preserve differences until the user commits a unifying value.
- Invalid: retain the user’s draft separately, state the violated rule, and offer specific repair without replacing committed data.
- Missing dependency: preserve the reference and editable intent, use a defined fallback, and provide locate, replace, or detach actions.
- Read-only or denied: explain the governing policy and keep inspection, copy, and export available where permitted.
- Offline or service unavailable: keep local authoring operational; queue only idempotent connected operations and display their state.
- Large selection or project: virtualize and batch presentation while keeping the mutation atomic and cancelable.

## XIX. Implementation Program

This part is normative. Module introductions establish scope; numbered requirements define verifiable obligations. Cross-cutting requirements in Quality Attributes and Testing apply even when not repeated in a module.

### 19.1 Architecture runway and technical spikes

Module code  1901

Defines prototype questions, decision criteria, timeboxes, throwaway versus production code, and ADR outputs.

#### Scope and Outcomes

- Primary objects: spike, hypothesis, prototype, benchmark, decision record, exit criterion.
- Primary user outcomes: validate canvas, persistence, layout, export, and sandbox approaches before scaling.
- Critical invariant: every spike ends with evidence and a decision; prototype shortcuts do not silently become architecture.
- The module includes authoring UI, model semantics, persistence, history, preview/export behavior, accessibility, diagnostics, migrations, and verification unless explicitly excluded.
- The module excludes connected-service implementation details that are not needed for local authoring; those are handled behind adapters and permission boundaries.
#### Behavioral Model

The model for architecture runway and technical spikes is authoritative and UI-independent. Editing uses a draft → validate → preview → commit sequence. A commit creates one transaction with an operation name, actor, timestamp, affected stable identifiers, and an inverse or restoration strategy. Background work consumes immutable snapshots and returns results tagged with the originating revision; stale results are ignored.

All controls show whether a value is authored, inherited, calculated, unavailable, or mixed. When multiple selections are involved, the system computes the applicable subset before preview. It must not silently coerce incompatible objects. Removing a value restores the next valid source rather than writing a visually similar literal.

#### States and Edge Conditions

- Empty: explain the first useful action and provide it directly; do not display a dead panel.
- Loading or computing: retain last valid content when safe, show bounded progress, and allow cancellation for user-initiated work.
- Mixed or partially applicable: identify the affected subset and preserve differences until the user commits a unifying value.
- Invalid: retain the user’s draft separately, state the violated rule, and offer specific repair without replacing committed data.
- Missing dependency: preserve the reference and editable intent, use a defined fallback, and provide locate, replace, or detach actions.
- Read-only or denied: explain the governing policy and keep inspection, copy, and export available where permitted.
- Offline or service unavailable: keep local authoring operational; queue only idempotent connected operations and display their state.
- Large selection or project: virtualize and batch presentation while keeping the mutation atomic and cancelable.

### 19.3 Milestone 1 — core visual authoring

Module code  1903

Defines canvas, selection, transforms, node tree, inspector basics, layout primitives, styling, history, and preview.

#### Scope and Outcomes

- Primary objects: milestone, feature slice, acceptance demo, quality budget.
- Primary user outcomes: build a responsive static page with direct manipulation and reliable undo.
- Critical invariant: all authoring primitives have deterministic model and canvas tests; preview parity is demonstrated.
- The module includes authoring UI, model semantics, persistence, history, preview/export behavior, accessibility, diagnostics, migrations, and verification unless explicitly excluded.
- The module excludes connected-service implementation details that are not needed for local authoring; those are handled behind adapters and permission boundaries.
#### Behavioral Model

The model for milestone 1 — core visual authoring is authoritative and UI-independent. Editing uses a draft → validate → preview → commit sequence. A commit creates one transaction with an operation name, actor, timestamp, affected stable identifiers, and an inverse or restoration strategy. Background work consumes immutable snapshots and returns results tagged with the originating revision; stale results are ignored.

All controls show whether a value is authored, inherited, calculated, unavailable, or mixed. When multiple selections are involved, the system computes the applicable subset before preview. It must not silently coerce incompatible objects. Removing a value restores the next valid source rather than writing a visually similar literal.

#### States and Edge Conditions

- Empty: explain the first useful action and provide it directly; do not display a dead panel.
- Loading or computing: retain last valid content when safe, show bounded progress, and allow cancellation for user-initiated work.
- Mixed or partially applicable: identify the affected subset and preserve differences until the user commits a unifying value.
- Invalid: retain the user’s draft separately, state the violated rule, and offer specific repair without replacing committed data.
- Missing dependency: preserve the reference and editable intent, use a defined fallback, and provide locate, replace, or detach actions.
- Read-only or denied: explain the governing policy and keep inspection, copy, and export available where permitted.
- Offline or service unavailable: keep local authoring operational; queue only idempotent connected operations and display their state.
- Large selection or project: virtualize and batch presentation while keeping the mutation atomic and cancelable.

### 19.5 Milestone 3 — data and interactions

Module code  1905

Defines CMS, bindings, forms, expressions, animations, overlays, runtime state, localization, and SEO.

#### Scope and Outcomes

- Primary objects: milestone, content model, runtime, interaction, locale.
- Primary user outcomes: build a localized data-driven marketing site with forms and motion.
- Critical invariant: dynamic output is type-checked, accessible, secure, and covered by browser workflows.
- The module includes authoring UI, model semantics, persistence, history, preview/export behavior, accessibility, diagnostics, migrations, and verification unless explicitly excluded.
- The module excludes connected-service implementation details that are not needed for local authoring; those are handled behind adapters and permission boundaries.
#### Behavioral Model

The model for milestone 3 — data and interactions is authoritative and UI-independent. Editing uses a draft → validate → preview → commit sequence. A commit creates one transaction with an operation name, actor, timestamp, affected stable identifiers, and an inverse or restoration strategy. Background work consumes immutable snapshots and returns results tagged with the originating revision; stale results are ignored.

All controls show whether a value is authored, inherited, calculated, unavailable, or mixed. When multiple selections are involved, the system computes the applicable subset before preview. It must not silently coerce incompatible objects. Removing a value restores the next valid source rather than writing a visually similar literal.

#### States and Edge Conditions

- Empty: explain the first useful action and provide it directly; do not display a dead panel.
- Loading or computing: retain last valid content when safe, show bounded progress, and allow cancellation for user-initiated work.
- Mixed or partially applicable: identify the affected subset and preserve differences until the user commits a unifying value.
- Invalid: retain the user’s draft separately, state the violated rule, and offer specific repair without replacing committed data.
- Missing dependency: preserve the reference and editable intent, use a defined fallback, and provide locate, replace, or detach actions.
- Read-only or denied: explain the governing policy and keep inspection, copy, and export available where permitted.
- Offline or service unavailable: keep local authoring operational; queue only idempotent connected operations and display their state.
- Large selection or project: virtualize and batch presentation while keeping the mutation atomic and cancelable.

### 19.7 Milestone 5 — collaboration and scale

Module code  1907

Defines version comparison, comments, optional collaboration, libraries, large-project performance, and enterprise controls.

#### Scope and Outcomes

- Primary objects: milestone, collaboration, scale fixture, policy, approval.
- Primary user outcomes: support teams and large sites without weakening local ownership or reliability.
- Critical invariant: scale budgets pass on reference hardware; conflict and permission behavior has adversarial tests.
- The module includes authoring UI, model semantics, persistence, history, preview/export behavior, accessibility, diagnostics, migrations, and verification unless explicitly excluded.
- The module excludes connected-service implementation details that are not needed for local authoring; those are handled behind adapters and permission boundaries.
#### Behavioral Model

The model for milestone 5 — collaboration and scale is authoritative and UI-independent. Editing uses a draft → validate → preview → commit sequence. A commit creates one transaction with an operation name, actor, timestamp, affected stable identifiers, and an inverse or restoration strategy. Background work consumes immutable snapshots and returns results tagged with the originating revision; stale results are ignored.

All controls show whether a value is authored, inherited, calculated, unavailable, or mixed. When multiple selections are involved, the system computes the applicable subset before preview. It must not silently coerce incompatible objects. Removing a value restores the next valid source rather than writing a visually similar literal.

#### States and Edge Conditions

- Empty: explain the first useful action and provide it directly; do not display a dead panel.
- Loading or computing: retain last valid content when safe, show bounded progress, and allow cancellation for user-initiated work.
- Mixed or partially applicable: identify the affected subset and preserve differences until the user commits a unifying value.
- Invalid: retain the user’s draft separately, state the violated rule, and offer specific repair without replacing committed data.
- Missing dependency: preserve the reference and editable intent, use a defined fallback, and provide locate, replace, or detach actions.
- Read-only or denied: explain the governing policy and keep inspection, copy, and export available where permitted.
- Offline or service unavailable: keep local authoring operational; queue only idempotent connected operations and display their state.
- Large selection or project: virtualize and batch presentation while keeping the mutation atomic and cancelable.

## XX. Governance and Appendices

This part is normative. Module introductions establish scope; numbered requirements define verifiable obligations. Cross-cutting requirements in Quality Attributes and Testing apply even when not repeated in a module.

### 20.1 Specification governance

Module code  2001

Defines source-of-truth ownership, versioning, change proposals, approval classes, conflict resolution, and publication.

#### Scope and Outcomes

- Primary objects: spec version, change request, approver, decision, superseded text, effective date.
- Primary user outcomes: propose and approve changes; trace implementation impact; publish a new baseline.
- Critical invariant: normative changes receive new revision history and impacted requirement/test mappings.
- The module includes authoring UI, model semantics, persistence, history, preview/export behavior, accessibility, diagnostics, migrations, and verification unless explicitly excluded.
- The module excludes connected-service implementation details that are not needed for local authoring; those are handled behind adapters and permission boundaries.
#### Behavioral Model

The model for specification governance is authoritative and UI-independent. Editing uses a draft → validate → preview → commit sequence. A commit creates one transaction with an operation name, actor, timestamp, affected stable identifiers, and an inverse or restoration strategy. Background work consumes immutable snapshots and returns results tagged with the originating revision; stale results are ignored.

All controls show whether a value is authored, inherited, calculated, unavailable, or mixed. When multiple selections are involved, the system computes the applicable subset before preview. It must not silently coerce incompatible objects. Removing a value restores the next valid source rather than writing a visually similar literal.

#### States and Edge Conditions

- Empty: explain the first useful action and provide it directly; do not display a dead panel.
- Loading or computing: retain last valid content when safe, show bounded progress, and allow cancellation for user-initiated work.
- Mixed or partially applicable: identify the affected subset and preserve differences until the user commits a unifying value.
- Invalid: retain the user’s draft separately, state the violated rule, and offer specific repair without replacing committed data.
- Missing dependency: preserve the reference and editable intent, use a defined fallback, and provide locate, replace, or detach actions.
- Read-only or denied: explain the governing policy and keep inspection, copy, and export available where permitted.
- Offline or service unavailable: keep local authoring operational; queue only idempotent connected operations and display their state.
- Large selection or project: virtualize and batch presentation while keeping the mutation atomic and cancelable.

### 20.3 Decision record template

Module code  2003

Defines context, forces, options, decision, consequences, validation, reversal, and status for architecture and product decisions.

#### Scope and Outcomes

- Primary objects: ADR, context, option, decision, consequence, validation, supersession.
- Primary user outcomes: record consequential choices; revisit when assumptions change.
- Critical invariant: decisions link to requirements and code boundaries; superseded records remain intact.
- The module includes authoring UI, model semantics, persistence, history, preview/export behavior, accessibility, diagnostics, migrations, and verification unless explicitly excluded.
- The module excludes connected-service implementation details that are not needed for local authoring; those are handled behind adapters and permission boundaries.
#### Behavioral Model

The model for decision record template is authoritative and UI-independent. Editing uses a draft → validate → preview → commit sequence. A commit creates one transaction with an operation name, actor, timestamp, affected stable identifiers, and an inverse or restoration strategy. Background work consumes immutable snapshots and returns results tagged with the originating revision; stale results are ignored.

All controls show whether a value is authored, inherited, calculated, unavailable, or mixed. When multiple selections are involved, the system computes the applicable subset before preview. It must not silently coerce incompatible objects. Removing a value restores the next valid source rather than writing a visually similar literal.

#### States and Edge Conditions

- Empty: explain the first useful action and provide it directly; do not display a dead panel.
- Loading or computing: retain last valid content when safe, show bounded progress, and allow cancellation for user-initiated work.
- Mixed or partially applicable: identify the affected subset and preserve differences until the user commits a unifying value.
- Invalid: retain the user’s draft separately, state the violated rule, and offer specific repair without replacing committed data.
- Missing dependency: preserve the reference and editable intent, use a defined fallback, and provide locate, replace, or detach actions.
- Read-only or denied: explain the governing policy and keep inspection, copy, and export available where permitted.
- Offline or service unavailable: keep local authoring operational; queue only idempotent connected operations and display their state.
- Large selection or project: virtualize and batch presentation while keeping the mutation atomic and cancelable.

### 20.5 Glossary and canonical terms

Module code  2005

Defines the product, editor, model, layout, runtime, collaboration, plugin, delivery, and quality vocabulary.

#### Scope and Outcomes

- Primary objects: term, definition, domain, alias, deprecated term.
- Primary user outcomes: use consistent language in design, code, tests, analytics, and support.
- Critical invariant: canonical terms appear in APIs and UI where appropriate; deprecated terms have migration guidance.
- The module includes authoring UI, model semantics, persistence, history, preview/export behavior, accessibility, diagnostics, migrations, and verification unless explicitly excluded.
- The module excludes connected-service implementation details that are not needed for local authoring; those are handled behind adapters and permission boundaries.
#### Behavioral Model

The model for glossary and canonical terms is authoritative and UI-independent. Editing uses a draft → validate → preview → commit sequence. A commit creates one transaction with an operation name, actor, timestamp, affected stable identifiers, and an inverse or restoration strategy. Background work consumes immutable snapshots and returns results tagged with the originating revision; stale results are ignored.

All controls show whether a value is authored, inherited, calculated, unavailable, or mixed. When multiple selections are involved, the system computes the applicable subset before preview. It must not silently coerce incompatible objects. Removing a value restores the next valid source rather than writing a visually similar literal.

#### States and Edge Conditions

- Empty: explain the first useful action and provide it directly; do not display a dead panel.
- Loading or computing: retain last valid content when safe, show bounded progress, and allow cancellation for user-initiated work.
- Mixed or partially applicable: identify the affected subset and preserve differences until the user commits a unifying value.
- Invalid: retain the user’s draft separately, state the violated rule, and offer specific repair without replacing committed data.
- Missing dependency: preserve the reference and editable intent, use a defined fallback, and provide locate, replace, or detach actions.
- Read-only or denied: explain the governing policy and keep inspection, copy, and export available where permitted.
- Offline or service unavailable: keep local authoring operational; queue only idempotent connected operations and display their state.
- Large selection or project: virtualize and batch presentation while keeping the mutation atomic and cancelable.

### 20.7 Release readiness master checklist

Module code  2007

Defines cross-functional evidence required for alpha, beta, release candidate, general availability, and hotfix releases.

#### Scope and Outcomes

- Primary objects: release stage, gate, evidence, approver, waiver, expiry.
- Primary user outcomes: assess readiness; record waivers; prevent incomplete promotion.
- Critical invariant: waivers are narrow, time-bound, owned, and visible in release notes and follow-up work.
- The module includes authoring UI, model semantics, persistence, history, preview/export behavior, accessibility, diagnostics, migrations, and verification unless explicitly excluded.
- The module excludes connected-service implementation details that are not needed for local authoring; those are handled behind adapters and permission boundaries.
#### Behavioral Model

The model for release readiness master checklist is authoritative and UI-independent. Editing uses a draft → validate → preview → commit sequence. A commit creates one transaction with an operation name, actor, timestamp, affected stable identifiers, and an inverse or restoration strategy. Background work consumes immutable snapshots and returns results tagged with the originating revision; stale results are ignored.

All controls show whether a value is authored, inherited, calculated, unavailable, or mixed. When multiple selections are involved, the system computes the applicable subset before preview. It must not silently coerce incompatible objects. Removing a value restores the next valid source rather than writing a visually similar literal.

#### States and Edge Conditions

- Empty: explain the first useful action and provide it directly; do not display a dead panel.
- Loading or computing: retain last valid content when safe, show bounded progress, and allow cancellation for user-initiated work.
- Mixed or partially applicable: identify the affected subset and preserve differences until the user commits a unifying value.
- Invalid: retain the user’s draft separately, state the violated rule, and offer specific repair without replacing committed data.
- Missing dependency: preserve the reference and editable intent, use a defined fallback, and provide locate, replace, or detach actions.
- Read-only or denied: explain the governing policy and keep inspection, copy, and export available where permitted.
- Offline or service unavailable: keep local authoring operational; queue only idempotent connected operations and display their state.
- Large selection or project: virtualize and batch presentation while keeping the mutation atomic and cancelable.

## Appendix A — Initial Performance Budgets

These budgets are baseline release targets and must be revalidated against named hardware before each release. P95 applies after warm-up unless specified. A budget change requires benchmark evidence and approval; it is not an acceptable response to a regression by itself.

| Operation | Target | Hard ceiling | Measurement conditions |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Cold launch to editable window | ≤ 2.5 s | 4.0 s | Reference Apple silicon Mac; recent project disabled |
| Open standard project | ≤ 1.5 s | 3.0 s | 1,000 nodes; assets cached |
| Open large project | ≤ 5.0 s | 10.0 s | 10,000 nodes; 500 assets |
| Pointer-to-canvas feedback | ≤ 16 ms | 33 ms | Active transform; overlays enabled |
| Inspector commit feedback | ≤ 50 ms | 100 ms | Single selection; local validation |
| Undo or redo | ≤ 100 ms | 250 ms | Standard transaction |
| Autosave foreground interruption | 0 dropped frames | 1 frame | Journal flush scheduled off main actor |
| Incremental preview update | ≤ 250 ms | 750 ms | One-page local change |
| Incremental production build | ≤ 2 s | 5 s | Single-page style/content change |
| Memory, standard project | ≤ 1.0 GB | 1.5 GB | 30-minute representative workflow |
| Memory, large project | ≤ 2.5 GB | 4.0 GB | 10,000-node fixture |
| Crash-free editing sessions | ≥ 99.9% | 99.5% | Eligible opted-in sessions; privacy-filtered |

## Appendix B — Security Threat Baseline

| Boundary | Representative threats | Mandatory controls |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Untrusted project package | Malformed archives, parser exploits, path traversal, decompression bombs | Validate before extraction; size and count limits; canonicalized paths; sandboxed decoders; fuzz tests |
| Custom code and embeds | Editor privilege escalation, data exfiltration, persistent script execution | Separate preview process; CSP; origin isolation; explicit permissions; no editor bridge by default |
| Plugins | Supply-chain compromise, overbroad file/network access, UI spoofing | Signing and provenance; capability grants; sandbox; revocation; safe mode; audit log |
| Publishing credentials | Secret leakage into project, logs, export, or support bundle | Keychain or service-side vault references; redaction; least privilege; rotation |
| Collaboration | Unauthorized reads/writes, replay, confused deputy, malicious payloads | Server authorization; signed sessions; schema validation; rate limits; audit; conflict safety |
| Generated websites | XSS, unsafe URL schemes, dependency vulnerabilities, insecure forms | Context-aware escaping; scheme allowlist; dependency scanning; CSP guidance; secure submission adapters |
| Update system | Malicious or rollback update, feed compromise | Signed updates; TLS; version monotonicity policy; notarization; staged rollout |
| Diagnostics | Accidental collection of content, secrets, personal data | Structured allowlist logging; redaction; consented content inclusion; retention limits |

## Appendix C — Accessibility Authoring Checklist

### Editor application

☐ All functions reachable by keyboard and exposed in menus or command palette

☐ Logical focus order; focus retained or intentionally restored after mutations

☐ VoiceOver names, roles, values, states, actions, and announcements for custom controls

☐ Canvas offers semantic navigation and property editing alternatives to direct manipulation

☐ Text and icons meet contrast requirements; meaning is not conveyed by color alone

☐ Reduce Motion and Reduce Transparency respected; zoom and text scaling do not clip controls

### Generated site

☐ Landmarks and semantic elements match intent

☐ Heading outline is ordered and diagnosable

☐ Images and meaningful vectors have alternative text; decorative media is excluded appropriately

☐ Forms have programmatic labels, instructions, errors, grouping, and focus management

☐ Keyboard interactions follow expected patterns and expose visible focus

☐ Motion, autoplay, time limits, flashing, and target sizes are audited

☐ Language, direction, title, and link purpose are present

☐ Automated checks are supplemented by keyboard, screen-reader, zoom, contrast, and cognitive review

## Appendix D — AI Implementation Work Packet Template

Use this template for every bounded AI-assisted change. Do not ask an implementation agent to “build the module” without the concrete contract below.

### Objective

One observable outcome, phrased in user and system terms.

### Requirement IDs

Exact SF-… identifiers implemented or verified.

### Allowed scope

Files, modules, APIs, and generated artifacts the agent may change.

### Forbidden scope

Adjacent behavior, schemas, dependencies, and visual systems that must remain unchanged.

### Context packet

Relevant model contracts, commands, design tokens, screenshots, fixtures, ADRs, and known constraints.

### Acceptance evidence

Tests to add or update, manual verification steps, performance measurement, accessibility evidence, and migration proof.

### Failure behavior

Invalid, empty, loading, cancellation, permission, offline, missing dependency, and recovery expectations.

### Review checklist

Architecture direction, data integrity, concurrency, security, privacy, accessibility, localization, performance, diagnostics, code clarity, and documentation.

### Completion record

Commit/PR, implementation owner, reviewer, requirement status, test links, known limitations, and follow-up IDs.

## Appendix F — Glossary

Authoring graph: Canonical editable project representation, including nodes, reusable definitions, data bindings, interactions, and metadata.

Computed value: Effective property value after defaults, inheritance, tokens, responsive overrides, states, and expressions resolve.

Definition: Reusable component source from which instances derive structure and defaults.

Editor overlay: Selection, guide, comment, presence, diagnostic, or drop affordance visible in the editor but excluded from published output.

Instance: Placement of a reusable component definition with stable identity and optional overrides.

Local-first: Core authoring and export remain useful with project data stored locally; connected services are explicit enhancements.

Node: Stable-identity object in the site tree, such as container, text, image, component instance, form, or embed.

Portable output: Standards-based HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and assets that can be hosted independently of SiteForge.

Preview: Isolated runtime execution of the current project revision using export-equivalent semantics and editor-only diagnostic bridges.

Project package: Atomic user-visible document containing the manifest, model data, local resources, indexes, and recovery metadata.

Requirement evidence: Test result, reviewed artifact, measurement, or manual record proving an acceptance criterion for a named build and environment.

Transaction: Atomic, named mutation boundary that validates changes, records affected identities, participates in history, and is durable or recoverable.

Work packet: Bounded implementation assignment containing requirement IDs, allowed scope, context, acceptance evidence, and review constraints.

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
